the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and أنتم is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ lā is negating; تعلمون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of أنتم. ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا﴾ a past verb; the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil and مثلا its object. ﴿عَبْداً﴾ badal (substitute) of مثلا. ﴿مَمْلُوكاً﴾ naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا يَقْدِرُ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is a second naʿt of عبدا. ﴿عَلى شَيْءٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقدر. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; man is conjoined to عبدا, and man is a relative noun. ﴿رَزَقْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنَّا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رزقناه. ﴿رِزْقاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿حَسَناً﴾ naʿt. ﴿فَهُوَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; هو is mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿يُنْفِقُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينفق. ﴿سِرًّا﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَجَهْراً﴾ conjoined to سرا. ﴿هَلْ﴾ an interrogative particle. ﴿يَسْتَوُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive by the lām; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to the omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ lā is negating, and يعلمون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar.

daas-irab:76-77.t: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا﴾ its i'rab has already been given; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿رَجُلَيْنِ﴾ badal (substitute) of مثلا. ﴿أَحَدُهُما أَبْكَمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of رجلين. ﴿لا يَقْدِرُ﴾ lā is negating, and يقدر is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلى شَيْءٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يقدر; the clause is a naʿt of أبكم. ﴿وَهُوَ كَلٌّ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), and mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿عَلى مَوْلاهُ﴾ ʿalā is a preposition; مولى is a noun, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra implied (muqaddara) on the alif owing to impossibility; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to كل. ﴿أَيْنَما﴾ a non-jussive conditional noun, an adverb of place attached to what follows it. [Translator's note: أينما is a jussive conditional noun — it makes يوجهه and يأت jussive, as the source itself goes on to say; the source writes «غير جازم» (non-jussive) as written.] ﴿يُوَجِّهْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); its fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of genitive by the construct (iḍāfa). ﴿لا يَأْتِ﴾ lā is negating; يأت is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a condition not joined to the fāʾ. ﴿بِخَيْرٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأت. ﴿هَلْ﴾ an interrogative particle. ﴿يَسْتَوِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ owing to heaviness; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿هُوَ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) of the fāʿil. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a relative noun, conjoined to the latent pronoun in يستوي. ﴿يَأْمُرُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِالْعَدْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأمر. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl; هو is mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلى صِراطٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar. ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ naʿt of صراط; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; لله: the Name of Majesty is genitive by the lām; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to an omitted, fronted khabar. ﴿غَيْبُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السموات. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; mā is negating. ﴿أَمْرُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿السَّاعَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿كَلَمْحِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿الْبَصَرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿هُوَ أَقْرَبُ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of inna; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:78-79.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَخْرَجَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ بُطُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أخرجكم. ﴿أُمَّهاتِكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَجَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جعل. ﴿السَّمْعَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالْأَبْصارَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السمع. ﴿وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ﴾ also conjoined. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun. ﴿تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿أَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation and lam is jussive. ﴿يَرَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَى الطَّيْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يروا. ﴿مُسَخَّراتٍ﴾ ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿فِي جَوِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مسخرات. ﴿السَّماءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿يُمْسِكُهُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and its object. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ inna, a particle resembling the verb. ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾ ذا is a demonstrative, the lām is for distance and the kāf for address; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿لَآياتٍ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and آيات is the noun of inna. ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of آيات. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. [Translator's note: in the parallel verses the source treats this clause as a naʿt of قوم; here it says "resumptive" as written.]

daas-irab:80-81.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿جَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) جعل. ﴿مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جعل; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿سَكَناً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ جُلُودِ﴾ its i'rab is like the one before it. ﴿الْأَنْعامِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بُيُوتاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَسْتَخِفُّونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of بيوتا. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to what precedes it. ﴿ظَعْنِكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَيَوْمَ إِقامَتِكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes, and its i'rab is like its i'rab. ﴿وَمِنْ أَصْوافِها﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to جلود الأنعام. ﴿وَأَوْبارِها﴾ conjoined to أصوافها. ﴿وَأَشْعارِها﴾ conjoined to what has gone before. ﴿أَثاثاً﴾ conjoined to بيوتا, i.e. "He made for you from their wool furnishings"; so it is a case of conjoining an accusative to its like. ﴿وَمَتاعاً﴾ conjoined to أثاثا. ﴿إِلى حِينٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to متاعا. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ. ﴿جَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the verb. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ min and the relative mā, attached to the verb. ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿ظِلالًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الْجِبالِ أَكْناناً﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and its object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعل; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ سَرابِيلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and سرابيل is its object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined. ﴿تَقِيكُمُ الْحَرَّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the kāf is its first object and الحر its second object. ﴿وَسَرابِيلَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes; the clause is a naʿt of the first سرابيل. ﴿تَقِيكُمْ بَأْسَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and its two objects. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿يُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object; its fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتم. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun. ﴿تُسْلِمُونَ﴾ the clause is the khabar, and the laʿalla clause is one of causation (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:82-85.t: ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive and in is conditional. ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾ a past verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾ the fāʾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), and innamā is the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿الْبَلاغُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْمُبِينُ﴾ naʿt (adjective); the apodosis of in is omitted, its implied form being "فلا غضاضة عليك" (then there is no blame on you). ﴿يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and نعمة is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يُنْكِرُونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَأَكْثَرُهُمُ الْكافِرُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and يوم is an adverb of time attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember). ﴿نَبْعَثُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نبعث. ﴿أُمَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَهِيداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لا يُؤْذَنُ﴾ lā is negating, and a passive imperfect verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to يؤذن. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلا هُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, lā is negating and هم is mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and idhā is an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿رَأَى﴾ a past verb; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative, fāʿil. ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response to idhā and lā is negating. ﴿يُخَفَّفُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb whose nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخفف; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is negating. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar.

daas-irab:86-90.t:
﴿وَإِذا رَأَى الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا﴾ its i'rab is like the one before it, and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) like it. ﴿شُرَكاءَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the response to idhā, with no grammatical position. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), with an omitted vocative particle, accusative (manṣūb) as a vocative; نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿هؤُلاءِ شُرَكاؤُنَا﴾ the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh) and أولاء is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject); شركاء is the khabar (predicate) and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of speech. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, naʿt (adjective). ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿نَدْعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the alif owing to impossibility; the clause is the khabar. [Translator's note: the verb ends in a wāw; the ḍamma would ordinarily be said to be implied on the wāw owing to heaviness. Translated as written.] ﴿مِنْ دُونِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأَلْقَوْا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَيْهِمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ألقوا. ﴿الْقَوْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar, nominative with the wāw, and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause is the object of speech. ﴿وَأَلْقَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to the one before it. ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive by the lām; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to ألقوا. [Translator's note: the preposition here is إلى; the source says «باللام» (by the lām) as written.] ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ يوم is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to ألقوا, and idh is an adverb of time in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿السَّلَمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَضَلَّ﴾ a past verb; the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ضل. ﴿ما﴾ a relative, fāʿil. ﴿كانُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَصَدُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to صدوا. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿زِدْناهُمْ عَذاباً﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿عَذاباً﴾ its second object. ﴿فَوْقَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to an omitted naʿt of عذابا. [Translator's note: فوق is normally classed as an adverb of place; the source says "of time" as written.] ﴿الْعَذابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِما﴾ mā — it and what follows it are in the position of genitive; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to زدناهم. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يُفْسِدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar.
﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and يوم is an adverb of time attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember). ﴿نَبْعَثُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِي كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نبعث. ﴿أُمَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَهِيداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شهيدا. ﴿مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of شهيدا; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَجِئْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿بِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جئنا. ﴿شَهِيداً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿عَلى هؤُلاءِ﴾ the hāʾ is for drawing attention and أولاء is a demonstrative in the position of genitive by ʿalā; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to شهيدا. ﴿وَنَزَّلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نزلنا. ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تِبْياناً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تبيانا. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَهُدىً﴾ conjoined to تبيانا. ﴿وَرَحْمَةً وَبُشْرى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes. ﴿لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بشرى. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَأْمُرُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿بِالْعَدْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأمر. ﴿وَالْإِحْسانِ وَإِيتاءِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿ذِي﴾ meaning "possessor of", in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the sign of its genitive is the yāʾ because it is one of the five nouns. ﴿الْقُرْبى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَيَنْهى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with the ḍamma implied on the alif owing to impossibility; its fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to يأمر. ﴿عَنِ الْفَحْشاءِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينهى. ﴿وَالْمُنْكَرِ وَالْبَغْيِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿يَعِظُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun; the clause is one of causation (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لعلكم.

daas-irab:91-92.t: ﴿وَأَوْفُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿بِعَهْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أوفوا. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿عاهَدْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is negating. ﴿تَنْقُضُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā, the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. [Translator's note: the lā here is prohibitive (nāhiya), as its jussive effect shows; the source calls it «نافية» (negating) as written.] ﴿الْأَيْمانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to تنقضوا. ﴿تَوْكِيدِها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial) and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿جَعَلْتُمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جعلتم. ﴿كَفِيلًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿ما﴾ a relative, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is prohibitive. ﴿تَكُونُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿كَالَّتِي﴾ التي is a relative noun in the position of genitive, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to an omitted khabar of تكونوا. ﴿نَقَضَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿غَزْلَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نقضت. ﴿قُوَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَنْكاثاً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿تَتَّخِذُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿أَيْمانَكُمْ دَخَلًا﴾ the two objects of تتخذون; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of دخلا. ﴿أَنْ﴾ the particle of the subjunctive (nāṣiba). ﴿تَكُونَ﴾ a defective imperfect verb; an and what follows it are mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿أُمَّةٌ﴾ the noun of تكون. ﴿هِيَ أَرْبى﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the clause is the khabar. ﴿مِنْ أُمَّةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أربى. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿يَبْلُوكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fronted object, and the Name of Majesty is its postponed fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يبلوكم [Translator's note: the source misspells it «ببيولكم»]. ﴿وَلَيُبَيِّنَنَّ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām occurs in the response to an oath, and an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يبين. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ما﴾ a relative, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تختلفون. ﴿تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ the clause is the khabar.

daas-irab:93-95.t: ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and law is a non-jussive conditional. ﴿شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لَجَعَلَكُمْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to law, and a past verb and its object; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أُمَّةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿واحِدَةً﴾ naʿt (adjective); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial) and lākin is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿يُضِلُّ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative, mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes, and its i'rab is like its i'rab. ﴿وَلَتُسْئَلُنَّ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the nūn was deleted owing to the dislike of a succession of identical letters, and the wāw was deleted owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause has no grammatical position, and the oath and its response are resumptive. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ composed of ʿan and the relative mā; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) لتسألن. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿وَلا تَتَّخِذُوا﴾ the wāw is resumptive and lā is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿أَيْمانَكُمْ دَخَلًا﴾ the two objects of تتخذوا; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to دخلا; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَتَزِلَّ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ of causation. ﴿قَدَمٌ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb attached to تزل. ﴿ثُبُوتِها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَتَذُوقُوا﴾ conjoined to تزل and accusative like it, by the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿السُّوءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِما﴾ mā is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya). ﴿صَدَدْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is genitive by the yāʾ, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to تذوقوا. [Translator's note: the source reads «بالياء» (by the yāʾ); «بالباء» (by the bāʾ) is evidently meant.] ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to صددتم. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلَكُمْ عَذابٌ﴾ لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar, and عذاب is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ naʿt. ﴿وَلا﴾ lā is prohibitive. ﴿تَشْتَرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined by the wāw. ﴿بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ﴾ بعهد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تشتروا, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ثَمَناً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ naʿt. ﴿إن﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿ما﴾ its noun. ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila; the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿هُوَ خَيْرٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is the khabar. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خير. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb; the clause is the khabar, and the apodosis is omitted.

daas-irab:96-97.t: ﴿ما﴾ a relative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عِنْدَكُمْ﴾ an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause); the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَنْفَدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿وَما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ باقٍ﴾ mā is a relative, mubtadaʾ; عند is the ṣila and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; باق is the khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ that was deleted owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters. ﴿وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the lām occurs in the response to the oath and the wāw is resumptive; the clause is resumptive, the clause of the response to the oath has no grammatical position, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿صَبَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَجْرَهُمْ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِأَحْسَنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نجزين. ﴿ما﴾ a relative in the position of genitive by the construct (iḍāfa). ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَمِلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿صالِحاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ ذَكَرٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَوْ أُنْثى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ذكر. ﴿وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the hāʾ is its object; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of apodosis and protasis are in the position of nominative as the khabar of man. ﴿حَياةً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿طَيِّبَةً﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object; its i'rab is like the i'rab of نحيينه, and it is conjoined to it. ﴿أَجْرَهُمْ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِأَحْسَنِ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ see its i'rab in the previous verse.

daas-irab:98-101.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and idhā is an adverb containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its response; the clause is resumptive. ﴿قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ﴾ a past verb and its object; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir) [Translator's note: the fāʿil of قرأت is the overt attached tāʾ; the source says "latent" as written]; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَاسْتَعِذْ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response to idhā, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ﴾ both are [prepositions with their genitive nouns] attached to استعذ. ﴿الرَّجِيمِ﴾ naʿt (adjective); the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun; the clause is one of causation (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَيْسَ﴾ operates like kāna. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the fronted khabar (predicate) of laysa. ﴿سُلْطانٌ﴾ the postponed noun of laysa; the clause is the khabar of إنه. ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is genitive, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to سلطان. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَلى رَبِّهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتوكلون; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿سُلْطانُهُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is in the position of genitive, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to the الذين before it. ﴿هُمْ بِهِ مُشْرِكُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the khabar. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and idhā is an adverb for future time, putting its condition in the genitive [as muḍāf ilayhi] and made accusative by its response. ﴿بَدَّلْنا آيَةً﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object. ﴿مَكانَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿آيَةً﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ and أعلم the khabar; the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾ mā is a relative; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to أعلم. ﴿يُنَزِّلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the response to idhā. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ kāffa wa-makfūfa. ﴿أَنْتَ مُفْتَرٍ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar, and the clause أكثرهم etc. is resumptive.

daas-irab:102-104.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿نَزَّلَهُ رُوحُ﴾ a past verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿الْقُدُسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) نزله; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لِيُثَبِّتَ﴾ the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; its fāʿil is latent; the lām and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) after it are attached to نزله. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَهُدىً﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو هدى" (it is guidance); the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿وَبُشْرى﴾ conjoined to هدى. ﴿لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بشرى. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿نَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause occurs as the response to an oath, with no grammatical position, and the speech is conjoined. ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ anna and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar standing in place of the two objects of نعلم. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ﴾ an imperfect verb, its object and its postponed fāʿil; the clause is the object of speech. ﴿لِسانُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يُلْحِدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يلحدون. ﴿أَعْجَمِيٌّ﴾ khabar. ﴿وَهذا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿لِسانُ﴾ khabar. ﴿عَرَبِيٌّ﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ a second naʿt; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative, the noun of inna. ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِآياتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤمنون. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا يَهْدِيهِمُ اللَّهُ﴾ lā is negating, and يهديهم is an imperfect verb and its fronted object, and the Name of Majesty is its postponed fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ naʿt; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:105-106.t: ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿يَفْتَرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ owing to heaviness; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الْكَذِبَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil (agent). ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِآياتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يؤمنون. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَأُولئِكَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and أولاء is a demonstrative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), with no grammatical position. ﴿الْكاذِبُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate), nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَفَرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive by the bāʾ; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to كفر. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كفر. ﴿إِيمانِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun in the position of accusative as the excepted (mustathnā). ﴿أُكْرِهَ﴾ a passive past verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and lākin is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿شَرَحَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿بِالْكُفْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شرح. ﴿صَدْراً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿فَعَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿غَضَبٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive by min; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of غضب; the clause of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is in the position of jussive. ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ naʿt; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:124-125.t: ﴿إِنَّما﴾: kāffa and makfūfa (the restraining mā and the restrained particle). ﴿جُعِلَ السَّبْتُ﴾: a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to جعل. ﴿اخْتَلَفُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِيهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to what precedes, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; inna and its noun, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَيَحْكُمُ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Translator's note: so in the source; there is no kāf in يحكم], and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: an adverb of place attached to يحكم, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time attached to يحكم. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِيما﴾: mā is a relative noun, and the two (preposition and noun) are attached to يحكم. ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِيهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to what follows. ﴿يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿ادْعُ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلى سَبِيلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ادع. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِالْحِكْمَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ادع. ﴿وَالْمَوْعِظَةِ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الحكمة. ﴿الْحَسَنَةِ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَجادِلْهُمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِالَّتِي﴾: a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the two are attached to جادلهم. ﴿هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾: inna and its noun, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿بِمَنْ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the genitive, and the two are attached to أعلم. ﴿ضَلَّ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ضل. ﴿وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعلم.

daas-irab:126-128.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and in is a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive. ﴿عاقَبْتُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); it is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis), and its clause has no grammatical position. ﴿فَعاقِبُوا﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis). ﴿بِمِثْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to عاقبوا. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عُوقِبْتُمْ﴾: a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and in is conditional. ﴿صَبَرْتُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the conditional clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿فهو﴾ ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ. ﴿لِلصَّابِرِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خير. ﴿وَاصْبِرْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and mā is negative. ﴿صَبْرُكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ; the two are attached to the omitted khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and lā is prohibitive. ﴿تَحْزَنْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تحزن, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿تَكُ﴾: an imperfect incomplete (nāqiṣ) verb, jussive by lā, the nūn having been deleted for lightness; its noun is omitted. ﴿فِي ضَيْقٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿مِمَّا﴾: mā is a relative noun, and the two are attached to an omitted adjective of ضيق. ﴿يَمْكُرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: inna, and the Divine Name is its noun; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿مَعَ﴾: an adverb of place attached to the omitted khabar of inna. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اتَّقَوْا﴾: the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is a relative noun conjoined to الذين, and it is in the position of the genitive like it. ﴿هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar, nominative by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:107-110.t: ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ ذا is a demonstrative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf for address; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمُ﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, and anna and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate); the hāʾ is in the position of accusative as the noun of inna, and the mīm is for the plural. [Translator's note: the particle is أنّ (anna); the source says «اسم إن» as written.] ﴿اسْتَحَبُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿الْحَياةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿عَلَى الْآخِرَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استحبوا. ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and anna, with the Name of Majesty as its noun; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لا يَهْدِي﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ owing to heaviness. ﴿الْقَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْكافِرِينَ﴾ naʿt. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ أولاء is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative, khabar. ﴿طَبَعَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to طبع. ﴿وَسَمْعِهِمْ﴾ [وَأَبْصارِهِمْ]: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes. ﴿وَأُولئِكَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and أولاء is mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf for address; the clause is conjoined. ﴿هُمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْغافِلُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is the khabar of أولئك. ﴿لا جَرَمَ﴾ a past verb meaning "it is established" (thabata). ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ anna and its noun; anna and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar, the fāʿil of لا جرم, i.e. "their loss is established". ﴿فِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to الخاسرون. ﴿هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is the khabar of أنهم. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, genitive by the lām, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to the khabar of inna. ﴿هاجَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to هاجروا. ﴿ما﴾ maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), i.e. "after their being tried". ﴿فُتِنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; together with ﴿ما﴾ it is interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ثُمَّ جاهَدُوا وَصَبَرُوا﴾ the past verbs are conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and غفور رحيم are the two khabars of inna, both nominative.

daas-irab:111-112.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember); the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَأْتِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the alif owing to heaviness. [Translator's note: the verb ends in a yāʾ; the source says "on the alif" as written.] ﴿كُلُّ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تُجادِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. ﴿عَنْ نَفْسِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجادل; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَتُوَفَّى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and توفى is a passive imperfect verb, nominative with the ḍamma implied on the alif owing to impossibility; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿كُلُّ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ما﴾ a relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿عَمِلَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl and هم is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿وَضَرَبَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and ﴿ضَرَبَ﴾ is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿مَثَلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قَرْيَةً﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿كانَتْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is omitted. ﴿آمِنَةً﴾ khabar. ﴿مُطْمَئِنَّةً﴾ a second khabar; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of قرية. ﴿يَأْتِيها رِزْقُها﴾ an imperfect verb, its object and its postponed fāʿil; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَغَداً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأتيها. ﴿مَكانٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿فَكَفَرَتْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِأَنْعُمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كفرت. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأَذاقَهَا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fronted first object. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿لِباسَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْجُوعِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْخَوْفِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿بِما﴾ mā is a relative, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to أذاقها. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَصْنَعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar.

daas-irab:113-114.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿جاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ﴾ a past verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa), and the clause of the response to the oath has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of رسول. ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَأَخَذَهُمُ الْعَذابُ﴾ the conjunctive fāʾ, and a past verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَهُمْ ظالِمُونَ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), and mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿فَكُلُوا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and كلوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ mā is a relative, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to كلوا. ﴿رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿حَلالًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) or ḥāl. ﴿طَيِّباً﴾ naʿt. ﴿وَاشْكُرُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿نِعْمَتَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿إِيَّاهُ﴾ an accusative pronoun in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted.

daas-irab:115-116.t: ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿حَرَّمَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَيْكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) حرم. ﴿الْمَيْتَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَالدَّمَ وَلَحْمَ﴾ conjoined to الميتة. ﴿الْخِنْزِيرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَما﴾ mā is a relative, conjoined to what precedes. ﴿أُهِلَّ﴾ a passive past verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is omitted; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لِغَيْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أهل. ﴿فَمَنِ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and man is conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿اضْطُرَّ﴾ a passive past verb whose nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿غَيْرَ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿باغٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا عادٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to باغ. ﴿فلا﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, and lā is the lā of generic negation. ﴿إثم﴾ its noun; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿عليه﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: these three words (فلا إثم عليه) belong to the parallel verse al-Baqara 2:173; the text of this verse reads ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ directly after ﴿وَلا عادٍ﴾. Translated as written.] ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ the two khabars of inna; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lā is prohibitive. ﴿تَقُولُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لِما﴾ the lām is a preposition and mā is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); it and what follows it are an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), genitive by the lām, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to تقولوا. ﴿تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. [Translator's note: تصف is an imperfect verb; the source says «ماض» (past) as written.] ﴿هذا﴾ the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh) and ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿حَلالٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَهذا حَرامٌ﴾ the clause is conjoined to the one before it. ﴿لِتَفْتَرُوا﴾ the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the wāw is the fāʿil; the lām and the interpreted maṣdar after it are attached to a badal (substitute) of لما. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive by ʿalā; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to تفتروا. ﴿الْكَذِبَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, the noun of inna; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive by ʿalā; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to يفترون. ﴿الْكَذِبَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا يُفْلِحُونَ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of inna.

daas-irab:117-119.t: ﴿مَتاعٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿قَلِيلٌ﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ naʿt. ﴿وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to حرمنا. ﴿هادُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿حَرَّمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾ a relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿قَصَصْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قصصنا. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قصصنا. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and mā is negating. ﴿ظَلَمْناهُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لكِنْ﴾ [وَلكِنْ]: the wāw is a conjunction and lākin is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ a fronted mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿رَبَّكَ﴾ the noun of inna; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿السُّوءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِجَهالَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تابُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تابوا. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ ذا is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿وَأَصْلَحُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the earlier إن ربك. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to غفور. ﴿لَغَفُورٌ﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and غفور is the khabar of inna. ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ a second khabar.

daas-irab:120-123.t: ﴿إِنَّ إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ inna and its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كانَ أُمَّةً﴾ kāna, whose noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, and أمة is the khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿قانِتاً﴾ a second khabar. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive by the lām, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) قانتا. ﴿حَنِيفاً﴾ a third khabar of kāna. ﴿وَلَمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lam is jussive. ﴿يَكُ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm); the nūn was deleted for lightness, and the noun of يكن is omitted; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿شاكِراً﴾ a fourth khabar of kāna. ﴿لِأَنْعُمِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شاكرا; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿اجْتَباهُ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَهَداهُ﴾ a past verb and its object; its fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلى صِراطٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to هداه. ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آتيناه. ﴿حَسَنَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), and inna, with the hāʾ as its noun; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar. ﴿لَمِنَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and min is a preposition. ﴿الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ genitive by min, and the two [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَوْحَيْنا﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. [Translator's note: the fāʿil of أوحينا is the overt attached pronoun «نا»; the source says "latent" as written.] ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوحينا. ﴿أَنِ﴾ maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya). ﴿اتَّبِعْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِلَّةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a diptote. ﴿حَنِيفاً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and mā is negating. ﴿كانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ kāna, whose noun is omitted, its implied form being "هو"; من المشركين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar; the clause is conjoined.

farraa:101-101.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا بَدَّلْنَآ آيَةً مَّكَانَ آيَةٍ﴾ (and when We substitute a verse in place of a verse): when We abrogate a verse in place of a verse that is gentler than it, the idolaters said: "He is only making it up himself and learning it from ʿĀʾish", a slave owned by Ḥuwayṭib ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, who had become Muslim and whose Islam was good, and who was a non-Arab. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:

farraa:103-103.t: His saying: ﴿لِّسَانُ ٱلَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ﴾ (the tongue of the one they allude to): they incline towards him and are fond of him, (أعْجَمِىٌّ) (is foreign). So Allah said: and this is the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ, and the Qurʾān is Arabic.

farraa:110-110.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ مِن بَعْدِ مَا فُتِنُواْ﴾ (then indeed your Lord, to those who emigrated after they had been put to trial): he says: (after) they were tortured. It was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and his companions who were tortured, until some of them uttered polytheism with their tongues while believing in their hearts; so Allah forgave them. That is His saying ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِن بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾ (indeed your Lord, after it, is Forgiving, Merciful): after the deed.

farraa:112-112.t:
His saying: ﴿قَرْيَةً كَانَتْ آمِنَةً مُّطْمَئِنَّةً﴾ (a town that was secure and at rest) means Mecca: it was not raided, as the Arabs used to do — they used to raid one another. (مُّطْمَئِنَّةً) (at rest): it did not move about, as the Arabs move in search of pasture by migrating.
His saying ﴿مِّن كُلِّ مَكَانٍ﴾ (from every place): from every direction. ﴿فَكَفَرَتْ﴾ (but it was ungrateful) — then He said ﴿بِمَا كَانُواْ يَصْنَعُونَ﴾ (for what they used to do) «[Translator's note: i.e. the feminine singular "town" is followed by a masculine plural referring to its people.]». There is much like this in the Qurʾān. Among it is His saying ﴿فَجَاءَهَا بَأْسُنَا بَيَاتاً أَوُهُمْ قائِلونَ﴾ (Our punishment came to it by night or while they were resting at midday), and He did not say قائلة. When He says (قائلون) He has the men in view, and when He says (قائلة) He means only its people; and His saying ﴿فحاسَبْنَاهَا حِسَاباً شدِيداً وعَذّبْنَاهَا عَذَابا نُكْراً فَذَاقَتْ﴾ (so We called it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment, and it tasted).
His saying ﴿لِبَاسَ ٱلْجُوعِ وَٱلْخَوْفِ﴾ (the garment of hunger and fear): they were afflicted with hunger for seven years, until they ate burnt bones and carrion. The fear was the expeditions and raiding parties of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then the Prophet ﷺ felt pity for them and sent them food while they were idolaters. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to them: eat ﴿وَاشْكُرُوا﴾ (and be grateful).

farraa:119-119.t: His saying: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ عَمِلُواْ ٱلسُّوۤءَ بِجَهَالَةٍ﴾ (to those who do evil in ignorance): everyone who does an evil deed is ignorant when he does it.

farraa:120-120.t: His saying: ﴿أُمَّةً قَانِتاً﴾ (an umma, devoutly obedient): a teacher (a marker) of good.

farraa:124-124.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ ٱلسَّبْتُ عَلَىٰ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ﴾ (the Sabbath was only imposed on those who differed over it): Moses came to his followers and said: "Devote yourselves to Allah on Friday and do no work on it." They said: "No, rather on Saturday, on which Allah finished creating the heavens and the earth." So it was made strict for them. Jesus also brought Friday to the Christians, and they said: "Their festival shall not come after ours", and so they turned to Sunday. That is their disagreement. It is also read (إنما جَعَل [98] «[Translator's note: "98" is a manuscript folio marker.]» السبتَ — with the accusative, i.e. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made (it)).

farraa:126-126.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ (and if you retaliate, retaliate with the like of what you were made to suffer) (it was revealed concerning Ḥamza): when the idolaters mutilated Ḥamza on the day of Uḥud, the Prophet ﷺ said: "I shall mutilate seventy elders of Quraysh." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾, then He commanded him to be patient, saying ﴿وَلَئِن صَبَرْتُمْ لَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لِّلصَّابِرينَ﴾ (but if you are patient, it is better for those who are patient); then He commanded him to be patient as a firm resolve.

farraa:127-127.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱصْبِرْ وَمَا صَبْرُكَ إِلاَّ بِٱللَّهِ﴾ (and be patient, and your patience is only through Allah), and His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِّمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ﴾ (and do not be in distress over what they plot): الضَّيق (ḍayq) is that by which your breast is straitened, while الضِّيق (ḍīq) is what occurs in something that can be wide, such as a house, a garment and the like. When you see الضَّيْق occurring in the place of الضِّيق, it is on one of two aspects: one is that it is a plural whose singular is ضَيْقة, as (the poet) said:
* كَشَف الضيْقة عَنا وفَسَحْ *
(He removed the straits from us and made room.)
The other aspect is that a "narrow thing" (شىء ضَيِّق) is meant, so it is lightened (by dropping the doubling), its origin being the doubled form, like هَيْن and لَيْن, by which you mean هيِّن and لَيّن (easy, gentle).

farraa:81-81.t:
His saying: ﴿سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ ٱلْحَرَّ﴾ (garments that protect you from the heat).
He did not say "the cold", although they protect from both heat and cold; it was left out because its meaning is known — and Allah knows best — as in the poet's words:
وما أدْرِى إذا يمَّمت وجهاً * أريد الخير أيُّهما يلينى
(I do not know, when I set my face in some direction seeking good, which of the two will befall me.)
He means: which of good and evil will befall me, because when he seeks good he is guarding against evil.
And His saying ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْلِمُونَ﴾ (so that you may submit): it has reached us from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read it as (لعَلكم تَسْلَمُونَ) (so that you may be kept safe) — from wounds.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ (they recognise the favour of Allah) means the disbelievers: when they are asked, "Who provides for you?", they say, "Allah", but then they say, "Through the intercession of our gods", and so they associate partners with Him. That is their denial of ( نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ).

farraa:86-86.t:
[His saying]: ﴿فَألْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ﴾ (but they will throw back the word at them): their gods will throw their words back at them: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ (indeed you are liars), i.e. "We did not call you to worship us."
And His saying: ﴿فَألْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ إِنَّكُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾: it (إنّ) takes kasra because it belongs to the ṣila (complement) of "the word" (القول). Whoever would give it fatḥa — had there been no lām in His saying لكاذبون — would make it an explanation of "the word": "they threw at them that you are liars" (ألقَوْ إليهم أنكم كاذبون), and it would then be in the accusative (naṣb), had there been no lām; just as you say: ألقيت إليك أنك كاذب (I put it to you that you are a liar). But only kasra is permitted once the lām comes in, so you say: ألقيت إليك إنّك لكاذب.

farraa:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّتِي نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا مِن بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ﴾ (and do not be like the woman who unravelled her spun thread after it was strong): "after strength" means after twisting it firm. She used to spin wool thread and twist it firm, and then order a slave-girl of hers to unravel it. It is said that she was Rayṭa. ﴿تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيْمَانَكُمْ دَخَلاً بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ (taking your oaths as a means of deceit among you): he says: as treachery (دَغَل) and deception.
His saying ﴿أَن تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرْبَى مِنْ أُمَّةٍ﴾ (because one community is more numerous than another): he says: it is greater in number. Its meaning is: do not betray a people because of their fewness and your great number, or your fewness and their great number, when you have lured them with oaths and they have come to rely on them. [97b] «[Translator's note: "97 ب" in the text is a manuscript folio marker.]» The position of (أدْنَى) «[Translator's note: so in the text; the verse has أَرْبَى.]» is accusative (naṣb). If you wish you may make it nominative (rafʿ), just as you say: ما أظن رجلاً يكون هو أفضلَ منك and وأفضلُ منك (I do not think any man is better than you): the accusative is on the basis of the ʿimād (the support pronoun, i.e. the separating pronoun), and the nominative is on the basis of making (هو) a noun (i.e. a mubtadaʾ (subject)). Similar is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللهِ هُوَ خَيراً وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْراً﴾ (you will find it with Allah, better and greater in reward) — accusative; had it been nominative it would have been correct.

farraa:1-1.t: His saying: ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَىٰ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ ("glorified and exalted is He above what they associate"). Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: ʿImād ibn al-Ṣalt al-ʿUklī narrated to me from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq Abū Sufyān, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Khaytham, that he read (سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالى عَمَّا تُشْرِكُون) ("above what you associate") — the first and the one after it, both with tāʾ. It is also read with yāʾ. Whoever reads with tāʾ, it is as though He addressed them; and whoever reads with yāʾ, it is as though the Qurʾān was sent down to Muḥammad ﷺ and then He said ﴿سُبْحانَهُ﴾, making him marvel at their disbelief and their associating partners.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿يُنَزِّلُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةَ﴾ ("He sends down the angels") with yāʾ, and (تَنَزَّلُ المَلائِكَةُ) ("the angels descend") with tāʾ. The reading of the companions of ʿAbdullāh is ﴿يُنَزِّل الملائكة﴾ with yāʾ.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلأَنْعَامَ خَلَقَهَا لَكُمْ﴾ ("and the cattle, He created them for you"). You put (الأنعامَ) in the accusative by "created them", since there is a wāw [before] "the cattle". So it is with every verb that returns to a noun by a pronoun referring to it, when before the noun there is a wāw, or a fāʾ, or speech that allows the verb to be transferred to that particle preceding the noun: there are two ways in it, the nominative and the accusative. As for the accusative, it is that you make the wāw a container (ẓarf) for the verb; and the nominative is that you make the wāw a container for the noun that is with it. Similar to it are ﴿وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾ ("and the moon We have determined for it phases") and ﴿والسَّمَاءَ بَنَينْاهَا بأَيْدٍ﴾ ("and the heaven We built with might"); and it is frequent.
Similar to it are ﴿وكُلَّ إنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ﴾ ("and every man We have fastened his fate to him") and ﴿وكُلَّ شىء أَحْصَيْنَاهُ﴾ ("and everything We have enumerated").
The proper way in the speech of the Arabs is to make kull nominative in these two words, whether or not there is a pronoun referring back at its end, because it is in the sense of "there is nothing but We have enumerated it in a clear register" — and Allah knows best. I heard the Arabs recite:

ما كلُّ مَنْ يظَّنُّنِى أَن مُعْتب * ولا كلُّ ما يَرْوَى عَليَّ أقول
(Not everyone who suspects me — I [will] placate, nor everything that is reported of me do I say.)

He did not make (أقول) fall upon the last kull, nor (مُعتب) upon the first. And one of them recited to me:

قد حَلِقت أَمُّ الخِيَار تَدَّعِى * علىَّ ذَنْبا كلُّه لم أصْنِع
(Umm al-Khiyār has taken to claiming against me a sin, all of which I did not commit.)

And one of the Arabs recited to me from Sūrat Yā Sīn: ﴿وَكُلَّ شَيىءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ فى إِمَامٍ مُبِين﴾ ("and everything We have enumerated in a clear register") in the nominative; he recited it so more than once.
As for His saying: ﴿وكلُّ شَىْءِ فَعَلُوهُ فى الزْبُر﴾ ("and everything they did is in the scriptures"), it can only be nominative, because the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: all their deeds are written in the scriptures. So it is nominative by fī, and (فعلوه) is a ṣila (relative clause) of "thing". Had fī been connected with faʿalūhu in speech like this, both the nominative and accusative of kull would be permissible; as you say: "Every man they beat in the house": if you mean "they beat every man in the house", you use the nominative or the accusative; and if you mean "everyone they beat is in the house", you use the nominative.
His saying: ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ﴾ ("in them there is warmth for you"): it is what is made use of from their hair. It was written without hamza because when what precedes the hamza is quiescent the hamza is dropped in writing; that is due to the faintness of the hamza when one pauses on it. Since what preceded it was quiescent and they could not pronounce its hamza in pause, their pausing was as though on the fāʾ. Likewise His saying: ﴿يُخْرِجُ الخَبْء﴾ ("He brings forth what is hidden"), ﴿النَشْأَةَ﴾ ("the creation"), and ﴿مِلْء الأَرْضِ﴾ ("the earth's fill"). Apply to the hamza what you found in these two words.
If in speech you wrote al-difʾ with wāw in the nominative, yāʾ in the genitive and alif in the accusative, it would be correct. That is on the basis of dropping the hamza and transferring the hamza's case vowel to the letter before it. Of that is the saying of the Arabs: "These are a true generation (nashʾu ṣidqin)"; when they drop the hamza they say: "These are nashū ṣidq", "I saw nashā ṣidq" and "I passed by nashī ṣidq". Better than that is to drop the wāw, the alif and the yāʾ, because their saying yasal is more frequent than yasāl, and masala more than masāla; likewise "between al-mar' [Translator's note: written «المَرِ», i.e. al-marʾ without its hamza] and his wife", when the hamza is dropped.
The benefits (al-manāfiʿ): their carrying them on their backs, their offspring and their milk. Al-difʾ: what they wear from them and build from their hair.

farraa:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ﴾ ("when you bring them home in the evening"), i.e. when you bring your camels home: you bring them back between the pasture and their resting place, which is called al-murāḥ. And al-surūḥ is in the morning (al-Farrāʾ said), when they go out to graze.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿بِشِقِّ ٱلأَنفُسِ﴾ ("except with great hardship to yourselves"). Most of the readers have kasra on the shīn, and its meaning is: except with the exertion of the selves. It is as though [al-shiqq] is a noun and al-shaqq is a verbal noun, just as it was imagined that al-kurh is the noun and al-karh the verbal noun. Some read it so: (إلاّ بِشَقِّ الأَنْفُسِ). It is also possible in His saying ﴿بِشِقِّ ٱلأَنفُسِ﴾ that you take the view that exertion diminishes a man's strength and himself until it makes him as though half of his strength had gone; so the kasra is on the basis that it is like the half. The Arabs say: "Take this shiqq", for a half of a sheep. And it is said: "The wealth between me and you is shaqq al-shaʿra and shiqq al-shaʿra (split down the hair)", and the two are close. When they say "I caused you hardship (shaqaqtu ʿalayka shaqqan)", they use fatḥa, and we have not heard anything else.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْخَيْلَ وَٱلْبِغَالَ وَٱلْحَمِيرَ﴾ ("and horses, mules and donkeys"): you put them in the accusative by referring back to "created". And if you wish, you make it accusative by implying sakhkhara ("He subjected"); its implication is then permissible like His saying: ﴿خَتَمَ اللهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعلَى سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهم غِشَاوَةً﴾ ("Allah has sealed their hearts and their hearing, and over their eyes is a covering") — whoever reads the accusative in al-Baqara puts "covering" in the accusative by implying (وجعل) ("and He placed"). Had you made ﴿ٱلْخَيْلَ وَٱلْبِغَالَ وَٱلْحَمِيرَ﴾ nominative, it would be correct in two ways. One of them is that you say: since the verb with them is not overt, I make it nominative by resumption. The other is to imagine that the nominative in "the cattle" would have been proper, and refer them back to that, as though you said: "and the cattle, He created them, and the horses and the mules", in the nominative.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لِتَرْكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةً﴾ ("for you to ride, and as adornment"): we put it in the accusative, and we make it "as adornment" by an implied verb, like ﴿وَحِفْظاً مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ﴾ ("and as protection against every devil"), i.e. We made it. Had there been no wāw with "adornment" nor with (وَحِفْظاً), you would put it in the accusative by the verb before it, not by implication. Similar to it is: "I gave you a dirham, and out of desire for the reward", the meaning being "I gave it to you out of desire". Were you to drop the wāw you would not need an implied [verb], because it is connected with the verb before it.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿وَعَلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾ ("and upon Allah is [showing] the straight path"). It is said: the guidance of the ways. And it is said: the path is Islam. (وَمِنْهَا جَائِرٌ) ("and of them are deviating ones"): it is said that the deviating ones are Judaism and Christianity. What indicates that this is the [correct] view is His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ لَهَدَاكمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ ("and had He willed, He would have guided you all").

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿تُسِيمُونَ﴾ means: you pasture your camels.

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِ﴾ ("ploughing through it"): its singular is mākhira, and it is the sound of the ships running with the winds; one says makharat, tamkhiru and tamkharu.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿وَبِٱلنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ ("and by the star they are guided"): it is said [this means] al-Jady (the Pole Star) and al-Farqadān.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ﴾ ("is He who creates like one who does not create?"). He used (مَن) for other than people since He distinguished it and placed it alongside the Creator, and that was proper; as He said: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِى عَلَى بَطْنِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِى عَلَى رِجْلَيْنِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِى عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ﴾ ("of them are some that walk on their bellies, some that walk on two legs, and some that walk on four"). The Arabs say: "The rider and his mount became confused to me, so I do not know which (man) is which (man)": since he combined the two and one of them was a human, (مَن) was proper for both of them together.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْيَآءٍ﴾ ("dead, not living"): you make it nominative by resumption. And if you wish, you refer it back as a khabar (predicate) of "those who", as though He said: "and those whom you call upon besides Allah are dead". "Dead" in this place [means] that they have no spirit in them, meaning the idols. And had it been accusative, on the basis of your saying "they are created dead", as qaṭʿ (cut off, i.e. ḥāl) and by the verb falling on it, i.e. "and they are created dead, not living" [Translator's note: the sentence is left without a conclusion in the text; the sense is "it would be permissible"].
His saying: ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ ("and they do not perceive when they will be raised"). He is saying: they are dead, so how could they perceive when they will be raised? — meaning the idols. And it is said of the disbelievers: "and they do not perceive when…". Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (إيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ) with kasra on the alif of (إيَّان); it is a dialect of Sulaym. I heard one of the Arabs say: "When is the īwān of that?", while [regular] speech is "the awān (time) of that".

farraa:30-31.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَنِعْمَ دَارُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾ ("and excellent is the abode of the God-fearing: Gardens of Eden"). You make "gardens" nominative because it is the noun [specified] for niʿma, as you say: "Excellent is the abode, an abode you dwell in". And if you wish, you make ﴿وَلَنِعْمَ دَارُ المُتَّقِينَ﴾ self-sufficient with what precedes it, then resume "gardens", so that its nominative is by resumption. And if you wish, you make it nominative by the pronoun referring back to it in ﴿يَدْخُلُونَهَا﴾ ("which they will enter").

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن تَحْرِصْ عَلَىٰ هُدَاهُمْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يَهْدِي مَن يُضِلُّ﴾ ("if you are eager for their guidance, Allah does not guide those whom He leads astray"). The companions of ʿAbdullāh read it (يَهدِّى), meaning: "the one whom He leads astray will not be guided (yahtadī)". The Arabs say of a man: "hadda al-rajul", meaning: he was guided (ihtadā). Similar to it is ﴿أَمْ مَنْ لاَ يَهِدِّى إلاَّ أَنْ يُهْدَى﴾ ("or one who is not guided unless he is guided?"). Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh, the brother of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, and Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ and others narrated to me from al-Aʿmash, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAlqama, that he read (لا يَهْدِى مَنْ يُضِل) likewise.
The people of the Ḥijāz read it (لا يُهْدَى من يُضلُّ) ("whoever He leads astray is not guided"), and that is a good way, because in the reading of Ubayy it is (لا هادى لمن أضل الله) ("there is no guide for whom Allah leads astray"). Man in both ways is in the position of the nominative: whoever reads ﴿يُهْدَى﴾ — it is nominative since its agent is not named [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]; and whoever reads ﴿لا يَهْدِى﴾ meaning yahtadī — the verb belongs to man [as its fāʿil (agent)].

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿بَلَىٰ وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقّاً﴾ ("yes indeed — a promise binding upon Him, true"): yes, He will surely raise them, as a promise binding upon Him, true. Had it been nominative, according to [a reading like] ﴿بَلَىٰ وَعْد عَلَيْهِ حَقٌّ﴾, it would be correct.

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا قَوْلُنَا لِشَيْءٍ إِذَآ أَرَدْنَاهُ أَن نَّقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ ("Our word to a thing, when We will it, is only that We say to it 'Be', and it is"). "Word" is nominative by His saying (أَنْ نَقُولَ), as you say: "Our word is only the truth". As for His saying ﴿فيَكُون﴾, it is accusative by being referred back to naqūla.
