Similar is the one in Yā Sīn, accusative, though most of the readers have made it nominative. Al-Kisāʾī used to reject the nominative in al-Naḥl [ms. 94b] and in Yā Sīn; yet it is permissible on the basis that you make ﴿أَنْ تَقُولَ لَهُ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the text, with tāʾ] a complete statement and then report that it will be, as you say of a man: "It only suffices him that I command him", and then you say: "and then he does (fa-yafʿalu) what he is commanded after that".

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُواْ﴾ ("and those who emigrated for Allah after they had been wronged"). It is mentioned that it was revealed concerning ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl and their like, who were tortured in Mecca. ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً﴾ ("We shall surely settle them in this world in a good place"): settling in Medina, and "We shall surely make the spoils lawful for them". The position of (الذين) is nominative.

farraa:43-44.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلاَّ رِجَالاً﴾ ("We sent none before you but men"), then He said: ﴿بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلزُّبُرِ﴾ ("with clear proofs and scriptures") after illā, whereas what is connected to what precedes illā is not put after illā. That is permissible on the basis of two statements. Of that is that you say: "None struck Zayd but your brother" and "None passed by Zayd but your brother". (If you say: "None struck [missing in ms. A] but your brother — Zayd", or "None passed but your brother — by Zayd"), it is on the basis of two statements: you mean "none passed but your brother", and then you say "he passed by Zayd". Similar to it is the saying of al-Aʿshā:

وليس مُجيراً إن أتى الحىَّ خائف * ولا قائِلاً إلا هو المتَعَيَّبَا
(He does not give protection if a fearful man comes to the tribe, nor does he say anything but what is shameful.)

Had it been a single statement it would be wrong, because "the shameful" belongs to the ṣila of "saying"; he placed it after [illā] and intended two statements, so that was permissible. And another said:

نُبِّئْتُهُمْ عَذَّبُوا بالنار جارتهُمْ * وهل يعِّذب إلاّ اللهُ بالنارِ
(I was told they tortured their female neighbour with fire — and does anyone but Allah torture with fire?)

I saw al-Kisāʾī treat (إِلاّ), with negation and interrogation, as equivalent to ghayr, putting in the accusative whatever resembles this as a single statement. He adduced the saying of the poet:

فلم يَدْر إِلاّ اللهُ ما هيَّجت لَنَا * أَهِلَّةُ أنآءِ الديار وشامُهَا
(None but Allah knows what the new moons over the distant abodes, and their marks, have stirred in us.)

But he has no proof in that, because (ما) is in the position of ayy ("which"), so it has an implied verb, on the basis of two statements. Yet his view is good: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿لَوْ كانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إلاّ اللهُ لَفَسَدَتَا﴾ ("had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would both have been ruined"), and he said: I find no meaning for it except "had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined". And he adduced the saying of the poet:

أبنى لُبَيْنَى لَسْتُم بيدٍ * إلاّ يدٍ ليست لها عضد
(O sons of Lubaynā, you are nothing but a hand — a hand that has no upper arm.)

He said: had the meaning been illā [as exception], the speech would be corrupt here, because in this verse I cannot repeat a genitive-governing particle with an implied [element]. And he has taken a [defensible] line here.

farraa:47-47.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ عَلَىٰ تَخَوُّفٍ﴾ ("or that He should seize them by gradual diminution"). The exegesis came that it is diminution. The Arabs say: taḥawwaftuhu, with ḥāʾ: I diminished it from its edges (ḥāfāt). This is what I have heard. But the exegesis has come with khāʾ (and it is a [valid] meaning). Similar to it, among what has been read in two ways, is His saying: ﴿إنَّ لَكَ فِى النَّهَارِ سَبْحاً طَوِيلاً﴾ ("you have by day a long occupation") and (سَبْخاً), with ḥāʾ and with khāʾ. Al-sabkh is ampleness. I heard the Arabs say: "sabbikhī your wool", which is like carding; and al-sabḥ is close to that. All are correct, praise be to Allah.

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلاَلُهُ﴾ ("its shadows turn"): the shadow comes back onto everything from its sides; that is its turning (tafayyuʾ). Then He explained, saying: ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَٱلْشَّمَآئِلِ﴾ ("to the right and the lefts"), making "right" singular and "lefts" plural. All of that is permissible in Arabic. The poet said:

بِفِى الشامتين الصخر إن كان هدّنى * رَزِيّة شِبْلَىْ مُخْدر فى الضراغم
(In the mouth of the gloaters be stones, if the loss of the two cubs of a lion in his den among the lions has broken me.)

He did not say "in the mouths of the gloaters". And another said:

الواردون وثَيْم فى ذُرَاسَبَأ * قد عضَّ أعناقَهم جلدُ الجواميس
(Those who come down [to water], and Taym, in the heights of Sabaʾ — the leather of buffaloes has bitten into their necks.)

And another said [ms. 95]:

فباست بنى عَبْس وأسْتَاه طيّء * وباست بنى دُودان حَاشا بنى نَصْرِ
(Shame on the rump of Banū ʿAbs and the rumps of Ṭayyiʾ, and on the rump of Banū Dūdān — except Banū Naṣr.)

So he used both plural and singular. And another said:

كلوا فى نصف بطنكم تعيشوا * فإنَّ زمانكم زَمَنٌ خميصُ
(Eat to half your belly and you will live, for your time is a time of hunger.)

The singular came because most speech is addressed to a single person: one says "take to your right and to your left", because the one addressed is one and so is the speaker. So it is as though, when he uses the singular, he has one of the people in mind; and when he uses the plural, there is no question about it. Likewise his saying:

بنى عُقَيل ماذِهِ الخنافِقُ * المالُ هَدْىٌ والنساء طالق
* وجبل يأوى إليه السارق *
(Banū ʿUqayl, what are these slanders? [Swear:] "The wealth is an offering, the women divorced", and a mountain where the thief takes refuge.)

He said ṭāliq [singular] because the administering of oaths mostly takes place between one disputant and another; so in the plural it ran on the most frequent usage in the original case. Similar is (بِفِى الشامتين) and the like.

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾ ("and to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, of creatures"). He said (مِن دابة) because (ما), even though it can take the course of (الذى), is indefinite (ghayr muʾaqqata); and when it is left vague and indefinite it resembles the conditional (al-jazāʾ). In the conditional, (مِن) enters an indefinite noun that comes after it; one says: "Whoever has struck him, of a man, strike him", and min is not dropped in this place. This is frequent in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿مَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ اللهِ﴾ ("whatever good befalls you is from Allah"); and He said: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثِى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ ("whoever does righteous deeds, of male or female, being a believer"); and He said: ﴿أَوَلم يَرَوْا إلى مَا خَلَقَ اللهُ مِنْ شىء﴾ ("have they not looked at whatever thing Allah has created"). In none of it did He say [it] dropping (مِنْ), disliking that it should look like a ḥāl (circumstantial) of man and mā; so they used min with it to indicate that it is an explanation of mā and man, because both are indefinite; so the entry of (مِن) into what follows them was an explanation of their meaning, and the entry of (مِن) indicated better what is indefinite in man and mā. That is why they were not dropped. Similar to it is the saying of the poet:

حاز لك الله ما آتاك من حَسَنٍ * وَحيثما يقضِ أمراً صَالحاً تكُنِ
(May Allah secure for you whatever good He has given you; and wherever He decrees a good thing, may you be there.)

And another said:

عُمْرا حَييت ومَن يشناكَ من أحد * يَلْق الهوان ويلق الذلّ والغِيَرا
(May you live long; and whoever hates you, of anyone, will meet contempt, humiliation and reverses.)

The coming of aḥad here indicated that he did not intend the indefinites that came [Translator's note: the text has «ن النكرات», evidently for «من النكرات»] to be ḥāl of the nouns before them, and indicated that it interprets the meaning of man and mā. Also indicating it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ شَىءٍ فَهُوَ يُخْلِفُهُ﴾ ("and whatever thing you spend, He will replace it"), because "thing" cannot be a ḥāl, but it is an interpreting noun. I only mentioned this because the Arabs say: "How excellent he is, of a man (min rajulin)!", and then they drop min and say: "How excellent he is — a man (rajulan)!" So "man" interprets (what precedes it) and is not a ḥāl; a ḥāl is only something that changes, like standing and sitting. You do not mean "How excellent he is in the state of his manhood only"; had you meant that, you would not be praising him with full praise, because when you say "How excellent you are, standing!", you only praise him in standing alone.
If you say: how then is dropping min permissible in this place? I say: because what precedes it is definite (muʾaqqat), so I did not mind it coming out, with min dropped, like a ḥāl; whereas in the conditional it was indefinite, and they disliked a ḥāl being explained from an indefinite noun, so they made min obligatory with it. If you say: [ms. 95b] the Arabs have said "mā atānī min aḥadin" and "mā atānī aḥadun", and allowed themselves to drop min — I say: that was permissible since there is nothing before aḥad, or what is like it, of which aḥad could be a ḥāl. That is why they said: "No man came to me (min rajulin)" and "No man came to me (rajulun)".

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلدِّينُ وَاصِباً﴾ ("and His is the religion, constantly"): its meaning is "perpetually". One says: waṣaba, yaṣibu: it lasted. And it is said: "purely".

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ ("and whatever blessing you have, it is from Allah"). (ما) is in the sense of a conditional and has an implied verb, as though you said: "Whatever blessing there is (yakun) with you is from Allah", because the conditional must have a jussive verb: if it is overt it is jussive, and if it is not overt it is implied, as the poet said:

إنِ العَقْلُ فى أموالنا لا نضِق به * ذِراعاً وإن صبراً فنَعْرِفُ للصبر
(If blood-money is [demanded] from our wealth, we are not distressed by it; and if [the demand is for] endurance, we know how to endure.)

He meant "if there be (in yakun)", and implied it. Had you made (ما بكم) in the sense of (الذى) it would be permissible, making (بِكُم) its ṣila (relative clause), and (ما) would then be in the position of the nominative by His saying ﴿فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, the fāʾ being brought in as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ المَوْتَ الذِى تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فإنَّهُ مُلاَقِيكُم﴾ ("say: the death from which you flee will surely meet you"). With every relative noun, such as man, mā and alladhī, the entry of fāʾ into its khabar (predicate) is permissible, because it resembles the conditional, and the conditional may be answered with fāʾ. But "Your brother, so he is standing" is not permissible, because it is not a relative noun; likewise "Your property (mālu-ka) is mine". But if you say "What you have (mā laka)", it is permissible to say [Translator's note: the text has «جاز أنت قول», evidently for «جاز أن تقول»]: "then it is mine"; and if you drop the fāʾ it is correct. Whatever you meet, judge it by analogy with this. Likewise an indefinite noun with a ṣila: you say: "A man who speaks the truth — then he is dearer to me than one who speaks falsehood". Dropping the fāʾ is better in all of it than bringing it in.
Al-juʾār is a loud voice. Of an ox one says: jaʾara, yajʾaru, juʾāran, when its voice rises from hunger or something else — with jīm. Likewise ﴿فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْأَرُونَ﴾ ("then to Him you cry out").

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ ٱلْبَنَاتِ سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ ("and they assign daughters to Allah — glory be to Him!"): [سبحانه is] accusative because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it carries a sense of seeking refuge and declaring Allah, Mighty and Majestic, free [of such things]. So it is like His saying ﴿مَعَاذَ اللهِ﴾ ("Allah forbid") and like ﴿غَفْرَانَكَ رَبَنَا﴾ ("Your forgiveness, our Lord").
His saying: ﴿لَهُمْ مَّا يَشْتَهُونَ﴾ ("and for themselves what they desire"): (ما) is in the position of the nominative. Had it been accusative, on the basis of "and they assign to themselves what they desire", that would be correct. I only chose the nominative because in speech like this one puts "to themselves (li-anfusihim)" in the place of "to them (lahum)" — do you not see that you say "You have assigned to yourself such-and-such", and you do not say "You have assigned to you"? With every verb or preposition that you mention from a pronoun and that returns upon it as a pronoun, make its second genitive [object] with nafs; so you say "You are for yourself, not for others"; then in the accusative you say "You killed yourself", and in the nominative "Your self destroyed you"; and you do not say ahlaktaka ("you destroyed you"). By bringing in nafs he only intended to distinguish between the self of the speaker and others. But when the verb falls from one pronoun onto another pronoun distinct from it, you do not bring in nafs. You say: "Your slave destroyed your wealth"; then you substitute pronouns for the slave and the wealth and say: "He destroyed it"; and you do not say "He destroyed himself" when you mean the wealth. The Arabs do say it with ẓanantu and its sisters raʾaytu, ʿalimtu and ḥasibtu: they say "aẓunnunī standing" (I think myself standing) and "wajadtunī righteous" (I found myself righteous), because of their incompleteness and their need for a predicate besides the noun. A poet, under constraint, may say ʿadimtunī and faqadtunī ("may I lose myself"); it is permissible, though rare. The poet said — he is Jirān al-ʿAwd:

لقد كان بى عن ضَرَّتين عدِمتُنى * وعمّا ألاقِي منهما متَزحزَح
هى الغُول والسعلاة حَلْقى منهما * مُخَدَّشُ فوق التراقى مكدَّح
(I had — may I lose myself! — a way to stay clear of two co-wives and of what I suffer from them. They are the ghoul and the she-demon; my throat, because of them, is scratched and bruised above the collarbones.)

farraa:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدّاً﴾ ("his face becomes darkened"). Had it been (ظلَّ وجههُ مُسْوَدٌ), it would be correct: you make the ẓulūl (becoming) belong to the man, and "face" and "darkened" are in the position of the accusative, as He said: ﴿وَيَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ تَرَىَ الذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلَى اللهِ وُجُوهُهُمْ مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ ("on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah, their faces blackened"). And the ẓulūl, when you say [ms. 96a] (مُسْوَدَّاً), belongs to the face.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ﴾ ("shall he keep it in humiliation?"). Al-hūn in the dialect of Quraysh is al-hawān (humiliation), and some of Banū Tamīm make al-hūn a maṣdar (verbal noun) for a thing that is light (hayyin). Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say: "You have been, since today, light (hūn) of provision indeed." And he said: I heard al-hawān in a similar sense from Banū Insān [Translator's note: so in the text]: he said: someone said of a camel of his: "There is nothing wrong with it except its hawān", meaning that it is cheap, light in price. When the Arabs say "So-and-so came walking ʿalā hawnihi (at his ease)", they only say it with fatḥa on the hāʾ, as in His saying: ﴿يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الأرْضِ هَوْناً﴾ ("they walk upon the earth gently"); it is tranquillity and dignity. Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Sharīk narrated to me from Jābir, from ʿIkrima and Mujāhid, concerning His saying ﴿يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الأَرْض هَوْنا﴾: they both said: with tranquillity and dignity. And His saying: ﴿أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ﴾ ("shall he keep it in humiliation or bury it [in the dust]?"): He is saying: he does not know which of the two he will do — keep it, or bury it in the dust. He is saying: will he bury her, or bear with her and with what he dislikes in her? She is the girl buried alive (al-mawʾūda). It is a parable struck by Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

farraa:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ مَثَلُ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾ ("for those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the evil description"). Had it been ﴿مَثَلَ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾ in the accusative it would be permissible; it would then be, in meaning, like your saying: "He struck for those who do not believe the evil description", just as in the reading of Ubayy: (وَضَرَبَ مَثَلاً كَلِمةً خَبِيثَةً) ("and He struck as a likeness an evil word"). The reading of the generality here and in Ibrāhīm is with the nominative; we have not heard anyone use the accusative.

farraa:62-62.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ ٱلْكَذِبَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾ ("and their tongues assert the lie that theirs is the best"). Anna is in the position of the accusative because it expresses the lie [i.e. it is a badal (substitute) from it]. And it might be said: ﴿وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ ٱلْكُذُبُ﴾, making al-kudhub an attribute of the tongues, its singular being kadhūb, [plural] kudhub, like rasūl and rusul. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولُوا لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الكُذُبُ﴾ ("and do not say, of what your lying tongues assert…"). Some put (الكَذِبَ) in the genitive, making it genitive by the lām in His saying (لِمَا), because it expresses (ما). The accusative in it is the proper way of the speech, and the generality read with it. Its meaning is: "and do not say, because of their asserting the lie…".
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ مُّفْرَطُونَ﴾ ("and that they will be abandoned"). He is saying: forgotten in the Fire. The Arabs say: "I left behind (afraṭtu) some people of them", i.e. I left them behind and forgot them. It is also read ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ مُّفْرِطُونَ﴾ with kasra on the rāʾ: they were going to excess in evil deeds against themselves, in sins. And it is read ﴿مُفرِّطُونَ﴾, as in His saying: ﴿يَا حَسْرَتَا عَلَى مَا فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ الله﴾ ("alas for my neglect in regard to Allah"); He is saying: in what I left and neglected.

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿نُّسْقِيكُمْ مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ﴾ ("We give you to drink from what is in their bellies"). The Arabs say asqaytu for everything that comes from the bellies of cattle, from the sky, or from a river flowing for a people. When a man gives you water for your lips, they say saqāhu, and they do not say asqāhu; as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَاباً طَهُوراً﴾ ("and their Lord will give them a pure drink"), and said: ﴿وَالّذِى هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِى وَيَسْقِينِ﴾ ("and who feeds me and gives me drink"). Sometimes they say both saqā and asqā for what is in the bellies of cattle and for rain-water, as Labīd said:

سَقَى قومى بنى مَجْد وأسقى * نُمَيرَا والقبائلَ من هلال
رَعَوه مُربِعاً وتَصيّفوه * بلا وَبَأٍ سُمَىَّ ولا وَبَالِ
(May He water my people, Banū Majd, and water Numayr and the tribes of Hilāl; they grazed it [the rain-fed land] in spring and summered on it, with no pestilence — it was named [so] — and no ill effect.)

The readers differed: some read ﴿نَسْقِيكم﴾ and some ﴿نُسْقِيكم﴾.
As for His saying ﴿مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ﴾ — He did not say buṭūnihā — it has been said — and Allah knows best — that al-naʿam and al-anʿām are one thing, and both are plurals; so the masculine refers back to the meaning of al-naʿam, since it stands for al-anʿām. One of them recited to me:

إذا رأيتَ أنجما من الأَسد * جَبْهته أو الخرَاة والكَتَدْ
بال سُهَيل فى الفضِيح. ففسد * وطاب أَلْبانُ الِّلقَاح وبَردْ
(When you see stars of Leo — its forehead, or its rump and its shoulders — Canopus has "urinated" into the milk-and-water drink, and it spoils; and the milk of the milch-camels becomes good and cool.)

He referred [the masculine "baruda"] back to "milk" (al-laban), because al-laban and al-albān have one meaning. Al-Kisāʾī said (نُسْقِيكم مِمَّا بُطُونِهِ): [i.e.] the bellies of what we have mentioned; and that is correct. One of them recited to me:

* مثل الفراخ نَتَقَتْ حواصلهْ *
(Like chicks whose crops have swollen.)

And another said:

* كذاك ابنةَ الأَعيار خافى بسالة الرجال وأصلال الرجال أقاصرُهْ *
(Thus, O daughter of al-Aʿyār, fear the valour of men; and the vipers among men are the shortest of them.)

He did not say aqāṣiruhum. Aṣlāl al-rijāl: the strong ones among them.
His saying: ﴿سَآئِغاً لِلشَّارِبِينَ﴾ ("palatable to those who drink"): He is saying: one does not choke on the milk nor gag on it.

farraa:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَوْحَىٰ رَبُّكَ إِلَىٰ ٱلنَّحْلِ﴾ ("and your Lord inspired the bee"): He inspired it by instinct (alhamahā), and no messenger came to it.
His saying: ﴿أَنِ ٱتَّخِذِي مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتاً وَمِنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ وَمِمَّا يَعْرِشُونَ﴾ ("take dwellings in the mountains and the trees and in what they construct"): these are the roofs of houses.

farraa:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿ذُلُلاً﴾ ("made easy") is a naʿt (adjective) of "the ways". One says "a dhalūl (smooth) way", and dhulul for the plural. And it is said that al-dhulul is an attribute of the bees, i.e. they were made submissive so that the drink comes out of their bellies.
His saying: ﴿شِفَآءٌ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ ("healing for people"), meaning that honey is a remedy. And it is said that in ﴿فِيهِ شِفَآءٌ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ the hāʾ means the Qurʾān: in it is the explanation of the lawful and the unlawful.

farraa:70-70.t: His saying: ﴿لِكَيْ لاَ يَعْلَمَ﴾ ("so that he knows nothing"). He is saying: so that he does not comprehend (شَيْئاً) ("anything") after his former understanding.

farraa:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿فَمَا ٱلَّذِينَ فُضِّلُواْ بِرَآدِّي رِزْقِهِمْ عَلَىٰ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ﴾ ("those who were favoured would not hand over their provision to those their right hands possess"). This is a parable Allah struck for those who said that ʿĪsā is His son — exalted is Allah high above what the wrongdoers say! He said: you do not make your slaves partners in what you own so that you are equal in it; so how have you made His servant a partner to Him, Blessed and Exalted?

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿وَحَفَدَةً﴾ ("and grandchildren"): al-ḥafada are the in-laws; and they said: the helpers. Had it been said al-ḥafad it would be correct, because their singular is ḥāfid, so it would be like ghāʾib and ghayab, and qāʿid and qaʿad.

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ رِزْقاً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ شَيْئاً﴾ ("and they worship besides Allah what has no power to provide for them anything from the heavens and the earth").
You put (شيئاً) in the accusative by the "providing" (al-rizq) falling on it [as its mafʿūl bihi (direct object)], as He, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَل الأَرْضَ كَفَاتاً أَحْيَاءً وَأَمْوَاتاً﴾ ("have We not made the earth a receptacle, for the living and the dead?"), i.e. it holds the living and the dead. Similar to it is ﴿أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِى يَوْمٍ ذِى مَسْغَبَة يَتِيماً﴾ ("or feeding, on a day of hunger, an orphan"). Had al-rizq been [annexed] to "thing", its genitive would be permissible: "has no power to provide them the provision of anything from the heavens". Similar to it is the reading of whoever reads ﴿فَجَزَاءُ مِثْلِ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ النِّعَمِ﴾ ("then the compensation of the like of what he killed, of cattle").
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ ("nor are they able"), while He said at the beginning of the statement (يَمْلِكُ) [in the singular]: that is because (ما) has the sense of a plural, for their gods which they worship; so (يَملك) was made singular according to the form of (ما) and its singularity, and it was made plural in (يستطيعون) according to the meaning.
Similar to it is His saying: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ﴾ ("and among them is he who listens to you"), and in another place: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُون إليك﴾ ("and among them are those who listen to you"). Similar is: ﴿وَمَنْ يَقْنُتْ مِنكُنَّ لِلّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتَعْمَلْ صَالحاً﴾ ("and whoever of you is obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does [fem.] righteousness") and ﴿يَعملْ صَالحاً﴾ [masc.]: whoever uses the masculine refers its end back to its beginning; and whoever uses the feminine takes the view that (مَن) stands in a feminine position, and so goes by its femininity. One of the Arabs recited to us:

هَيَا أُمَّ عمرو مَن يكن عُقْرَ دارِه * جِوَاءٌ عَدِىّ يأكلِ الحشرات
ويسودَّ من لفْح السموم جَبينُهُ * ويَعْرَ وإن كانوا ذوى نَكَرات
(O Umm ʿAmr, whoever has as the heart of his home the hollows of ʿAdī will eat vermin; his brow will be blackened by the scorching of the hot wind, and he will go bare, even though they are men of cunning.)

So in (كانوا) he returned to the plural meaning. And in the reading of ʿAbdullāh — as far as I know — it is (ومِنْكُمْ من يكون شُيُوخاً) ("and among you are those who become old men"), and he did not say (شَيْخاً). Al-Farazdaq said:

تَعَشَّ فإن واثقتنى لا تخونُنى * نكن مثل مَن يا ذئب يصطحبان
وأنت امرؤ يا ذئب والغدرُ كنتما * أُخَيَّيْنِ كانا أُرضِعا بِلِبان
(Have your supper; and if you pledge to me not to betray me, we will be, O wolf, like two who keep company. But you, O wolf, and treachery have been like two little brothers suckled at one breast.)

He made (يصطحبان) dual, though it is the verb of man, because he intended [the wolf] and himself.

farraa:75-75.t: His saying: ﴿ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً عَبْداً مَّمْلُوكاً﴾ ("Allah strikes a parable: a slave who is owned"). He struck a parable for the idol (al-ḍamm) [Translator's note: so in the text, here and below; evidently al-ṣanam, "the idol"] which they worship, that it has power over nothing. ﴿وهُوَ كَلٌّ على مولاه﴾ ("and he is a burden on his master"), i.e. he carries it. So He said: is this idol equal ﴿وَمَنْ يَأْمُرُ بالعَدْلِ﴾ ("to one who commands justice")? He said: do not make the idol equal to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

farraa:80-80.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّن جُلُودِ ٱلأَنْعَامِ﴾ ("and He made for you, from the hides of cattle, [tents]"), meaning tents for travel and the dwellings of the Arabs that are of wool and hair. Al-ẓaʿn ("travelling") is read heavy [i.e. ẓaʿan] and light, because its second letter is ʿayn; the Arabs do that with words whose second letter is one of the six [guttural] letters, like al-shaʿr, al-baḥr and al-nahr. One of the Arabs recited to me:

له نَعَل لا تَطَّبِى الكلبَ ريحُها * وإن وُضِعت بين المجالس شُمَّت
(He has a sandal whose smell does not attract the dog, and if it is set down among the gatherings it is sniffed [with pleasure].)

His saying: ﴿أَثَاثاً وَمَتَاعاً﴾ ("furnishings and enjoyment") — "enjoyment for a time": He is saying: they make do with their wool until they die. And it is said: [for] time after time.

muyesser-irab:56-56.t:
﴿ويجعلون لما لا يعلمون نصيبا مما رزقناهم﴾: conjoined to what came before; ويجعلون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يجعلون﴾; the clause ﴿لا يعلمون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position; the pronoun in يعلمون refers back to the polytheists, and it has been said: it refers back to the idols indicated by ﴿ما﴾; نصيبًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يجعلون; ﴿مما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نصيبًا﴾; and the clause رزقناهم is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿تالله لتسألن عما كنتم تفترون﴾: the tāʾ is the genitive-governing tāʾ of the oath, and the Divine Name is genitive (majrūr) by the tāʾ of the oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted, its implied form being "my oath (qasamī)"; the lām occurs in the answer of the oath; تسألن is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the presence of the nūn, which has been elided because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw, elided because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; ﴿عما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تسألن﴾; the clause ﴿كنتم﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position; and the clause تفترون is the khabar (predicate) of kāna.

muyesser-irab:57-57.t:
﴿ويجعلون لله البنات﴾: ﴿ويجعلون﴾: conjoined to what preceded. ﴿لله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يجعلون﴾. البنات: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يجعلون.
﴿سبحانه﴾: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); together with its omitted verb it forms a parenthetical clause, with no grammatical position.
﴿ولهم ما يشتهون﴾: ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿ما﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يشتهون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. It has been said: ﴿ما﴾ is in the position of the accusative by an implied (muqaddar) verb. The clause ﴿ولهم ما يشتهون﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; or the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of يجعلون.

muyesser-irab:58-58.t: ﴿وإذا بشر أحدهم بالأنثى ظل وجهه مسودا وهو كظيم﴾: إذا is a future adverb of time containing the sense of condition; the clause ﴿بشر أحدهم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿بالأنثى﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بشر﴾; the clause ﴿ظل﴾ has no grammatical position; وجهه is the noun (ism) of ẓalla, and ﴿مسودًّا﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the wāw is also circumstantial; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and كظيم a khabar, and the clause is an overlapping ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:59-59.t:
﴿يتوارى من القوم من سوء ما بشر به﴾: the clause ﴿يتوارى﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ﴿كظيم﴾; ﴿من القوم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) it, and ﴿من سوء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to it; the first [min] is for the beginning [of the action], and the second for cause; ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause بشر به is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿أيمسكه على هون أم يدسه في التراب﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; the interrogative clause ﴿يمسكه﴾ is governed by something omitted which is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of يتوارى, i.e. "he hides, perplexed"; يمسكه is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿على هون﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the latent fāʿil or from the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿أم﴾ is a conjunction; ﴿يدسه﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يمسكه﴾; and ﴿في التراب﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يدسه﴾.
﴿ألا﴾: a particle of alerting.
﴿ساء ما يحكمون﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿ساء﴾ is an inflexible past verb for expressing blame, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the fāʿil is a pronoun necessarily latent, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾. ﴿ما﴾: an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, in the position of the accusative as a tamyīz (specification) of the fāʿil of ﴿ساء﴾; the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "their judgement". The clause ﴿يحكمون﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ما﴾, the implied meaning being: "evil is it as a judgement that they judge".
Or ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun meaning alladhī, in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of ﴿ساء﴾, and the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "their judgement". The clause ﴿يحكمون﴾ is the ṣila of the relative, with no grammatical position.
Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). The clause ﴿يحكمون﴾ is the ṣila of the maṣdariyya ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. The interpreted maṣdar formed from ﴿ما﴾ and what it governs is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of ﴿ساء﴾, the implied meaning being: "evil is their judging". The one specified for blame is omitted.

muyesser-irab:60-60.t:
﴿للذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة مثل السوء﴾: ﴿للذين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); the clause لا يؤمنون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, a clause with no grammatical position; ﴿بالآخرة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يؤمنون﴾; and مثل السوء is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿ولله المثل الأعلى وهو العزيز الحكيم﴾: conjoined to what came before; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, العزيز a first khabar, and الحكيم a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:61-61.t:
﴿ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بظلمهم ما ترك عليها من دابة﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; لو is conditional; يؤاخذ الله الناس is an imperfect verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿بظلمهم﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition of causation, i.e. "because of their wrongdoing", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤاخذ﴾; the clause ﴿ما ترك﴾ has no grammatical position; ﴿ترك﴾ is a verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil; ﴿عليها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was [originally] an adjective of دابة; من is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and دابة is genitive (majrūr) in form and a mafʿūl bihi in position.
﴿ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative because it is lightened; يؤخرهم is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إلى أجل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يؤخرهم﴾; and ﴿مسمى﴾ is a naʿt (adjective), i.e. "appointed".
﴿فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive and the clause after it conjoined, or the fāʾ is resumptive and the clause after it resumptive, with no grammatical position; إذا is a future adverb of time containing the sense of condition; the clause ﴿جاء أجلهم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿لا يستأخرون﴾ has no grammatical position; ﴿ساعة﴾ is an adverb attached to ﴿يستأخرون﴾; ﴿ولا يستقدمون﴾ is conjoined to ﴿لا يستأخرون﴾.

muyesser-irab:62-62.t:
﴿ويجعلون لله ما يكرهون وتصف ألسنتهم الكذب﴾: the wāw is resumptive; يجعلون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يجعلون﴾; ﴿ما﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿يجعلون﴾; the clause يكرهون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position; ﴿تصف ألسنتهم الكذب﴾ is an imperfect verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; and the clause ﴿ويجعلون لله ما يكرهون﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿أن لهم الحسنى﴾: أن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh); الحسنى is its postponed noun (ism); ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of anna; and anna with what falls within its scope is a badal (substitute) of the whole for the whole from الكذب.
﴿لا جرم أن لهم النار وأنهم مفرطون﴾: لا is negating; جرم is a past verb; أن is an abrogating particle; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted fronted khabar; النار is its postponed noun; and ﴿أنهم مفرطون﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أن لهم النار﴾.

muyesser-irab:63-63.t:
﴿تالله لقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك﴾: the tāʾ is the genitive-governing tāʾ of the oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) verb of oath; the lām occurs in the answer of the oath; قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); ﴿أرسلنا﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إلى أمم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾; and ﴿من قبلك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective).
﴿فزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; زين is a past verb; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿زين﴾; الشيطان is the fāʿil, and أعمالهم the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فهو وليهم اليوم ولهم عذاب أليم﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ﴿وليهم﴾ a khabar (predicate); ﴿اليوم﴾ is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or attached to وليهم; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; عذاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and أليم a naʿt.

muyesser-irab:64-64.t:
﴿وما أنزلنا عليك الكتاب إلا لتبين لهم الذي اختلفوا فيه﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ما is negating; أنزلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿عليك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلنا﴾; الكتاب is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿لتبين﴾: the lām is for giving the reason, and ﴿تبين﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿أنزلنا﴾.
﴿وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون﴾: هدى and رحمة are conjoined to the position of ﴿لتبين﴾, and they are made accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); ﴿لقوم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective), or attached to the maṣdar; and the clause ﴿يؤمنون﴾ is a naʿt of قوم.

muyesser-irab:65-65.t:
﴿والله أنزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها﴾: ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause أنزل a khabar (predicate); ﴿من السماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزل﴾; ﴿ماء﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فأحيا is conjoined to أنزل; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أحيا﴾; الأرض is a mafʿūl bihi; and in ﴿بعد موتها﴾ the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يسمعون﴾: inna and its fronted khabar; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آية is the noun (ism) of inna; ﴿لقوم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿آية﴾; and the clause يسمعون is a naʿt of قوم.

muyesser-irab:66-66.t:
﴿وإن لكم في الأنعام لعبرة﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh); ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿في الأنعام﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and عبرة is the postponed noun (ism) of inna.
﴿نسقيكم مما في بطونه من بين فرث ودم لبنا خالصا سائغا للشاربين﴾: نسقيكم: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نسقيكم﴾. ﴿في بطونه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿نسقيكم﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿من بين فرث ودم﴾ is a ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of His words لبنًا and was placed before it; or it is a ḥāl from the ﴿ما﴾ preceding it; ﴿لبنًا﴾ is the second object of ﴿نسقيكم﴾; سائغًا is a naʿt; and ﴿للشاربين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿سائغًا﴾. [Translator's note: the source does not parse خالصًا.]

muyesser-irab:67-67.t:
﴿ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سكرا ورزقا حسنا﴾: ﴿ومن ثمرات النخيل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿تتخذون﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun which is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "fruit from which they used to take intoxicant and good provision". It has been said: ﴿من ثمرات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to something omitted indicated by ﴿نسقيكم﴾, i.e. "We give you to drink of the juice of date-palms and grapes", and the clause ﴿تتخذون﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It has [also] been said: they are attached to ﴿تتخذون﴾, and ﴿من﴾ was repeated for emphasis. It has been said: it is attached to ﴿نسقيكم﴾, so that it is conjoined to ﴿مما في بطونه﴾. And it has been said: it is conjoined to الأنعام, i.e. "and in the fruits of the date-palms and grapes there is a lesson", then He explained the lesson by His words: تتخذون. The pronoun in ﴿منه﴾ refers back to the implied juice; سكرًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of تتخذون; رزقًا is conjoined to ﴿سكرًا﴾; and حسنًا is a naʿt.
﴿إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يعقلون﴾: inna and its fronted khabar; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آية is its postponed noun (ism); and the clause يعقلون is a naʿt of قوم.

muyesser-irab:68-68.t: ﴿وأوحى ربك إلى النحل أن اتخذي من الجبال بيوتا ومن الشجر ومما يعرشون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive to what precedes it, or resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أوحى ربك﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إلى النحل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أوحى﴾. ﴿أن﴾: explicative, because revelation (waḥy) contains the meaning of saying without its letters, and the clause after it is explicative, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdariyya, and together with what it governs it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ﴿أوحى﴾; the clause ﴿اتخذي﴾ is the ṣila of the maṣdariyya ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position. ﴿من الجبال﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿اتخذي﴾, and min is partitive; ﴿بيوتًا﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿اتخذي﴾; ﴿من الشجر﴾ is conjoined to ﴿من الجبال﴾, and likewise ﴿مما يعرشون﴾.

muyesser-irab:69-69.t:
﴿ثم كلي من كل الثمرات فاسلكي سبل ربك ذللا﴾: ثم is a conjunction for delay; ﴿كلي﴾ is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿من كل الثمرات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كلي﴾; ﴿فاسلكي﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and اسلكي is conjoined to ﴿كلي﴾; ﴿سبل ربك﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿ذللًا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السبل, or from the fāʿil of ﴿اسلكي﴾, i.e. "while you are submissive to what you have been commanded".
﴿يخرج من بطونها شراب مختلف ألوانه فيه شفاء للناس﴾: يخرج is an imperfect verb; ﴿من بطونها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يخرج﴾; شراب is the fāʿil of يخرج; ﴿مختلف﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of شراب; ﴿ألوانه﴾ is the fāʿil of ﴿مختلف﴾, because it is an active participle which operates as a verb does; ﴿فيه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); شفاء is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿للناس﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿شفاء﴾; and the clause is a second naʿt of شراب.
﴿إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يتفكرون﴾: inna and its fronted khabar; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آية is its postponed noun (ism); and the clause يتفكرون is a naʿt of قوم.

muyesser-irab:70-70.t:
﴿والله خلقكم ثم يتوفاكم ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر﴾: ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause ﴿خلقكم﴾ a khabar (predicate); ﴿ثم﴾ is a conjunction for delay; ﴿ومنكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿منكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar, and it is conjoined to something implied, i.e. "so among you is one who remains retaining the strength of his body and mind, and among you…"; ﴿مَن﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause يرد is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa"; and ﴿إلى أرذل العمر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يرد﴾.
﴿لكي لا يعلم بعد علم شيئا إن الله عليم قدير﴾: the lām is the lām of giving the reason; ﴿كي﴾ is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; لا is negating; يعلم is accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿كي﴾; the lām with what it governs is attached to ﴿يرد﴾; or the lām is for outcome (ṣayrūra), i.e. "so that his end was that he returned to the state of childhood in forgetfulness and lack of perception"; ﴿بعد علم﴾ is an adverb attached to ﴿يعلم﴾; شيئًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يعلم, and it has been said: ﴿شيئًا﴾ is accusative by العلم; إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the Divine Name its noun (ism), عليم its first khabar, and قدير its second khabar.

muyesser-irab:71-71.t:
﴿والله فضل بعضكم على بعض في الرزق﴾: ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause ﴿فضل﴾ a khabar (predicate); بعضكم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿على بعض﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فضل﴾; and ﴿في الرزق﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "in the state of your being provided for, so among you is the rich and among you the poor".
﴿فما الذين فضلوا برادي رزقهم على ما ملكت أيمانهم﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negating mā which operates as laysa does; ﴿الذين﴾ is the noun (ism) of mā; the clause ﴿فضلوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; ﴿برادي﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿رادي﴾ is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and genitive by the bāʾ in form; ﴿رزقهم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), being an annexation of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its object; ﴿على ما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿رادي﴾; and ملكت أيمانهم is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿فهم فيه سواء﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ; ﴿فيه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿سواء﴾; and ﴿سواء﴾ is the khabar of ﴿هم﴾.
﴿أفبنعمة الله يجحدون﴾: an interrogation of disapproval and rebuke; the fāʾ is conjunctive to something implied (muqaddar), i.e. "they associate partners with Him and so deny His favour"; and ﴿بنعمة الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يجحدون﴾, because it contains the meaning of ingratitude (kufrān).

muyesser-irab:72-72.t:
﴿والله جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا﴾: ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause ﴿جعل﴾ a khabar (predicate); ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعل﴾; ﴿من أنفسكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and أزواجًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of جعل.
﴿وجعل لكم من أزواجكم بنين وحفدة﴾: conjoined to what preceded; ﴿من أزواجكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; بنين is the mafʿūl bihi of جعل, and حفدة is conjoined to بنين.
﴿ورزقكم من الطيبات أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمت الله هم يكفرون﴾: ﴿ورزقكم﴾ is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿من الطيبات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿رزقكم﴾; the hamza is for interrogation of disapproval and rebuke; the fāʾ is conjunctive to something implied, i.e. "they disbelieve in Allah and so believe in falsehood"; ﴿بنعمة الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يكفرون﴾; ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يكفرون a khabar. [Translator's note: the source does not separately parse بالباطل يؤمنون.]

muyesser-irab:73-73.t:
﴿ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لهم رزقا من السماوات والأرض﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; يعبدون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿من دون الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿ما﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿لا يملك﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; رزقًا is a mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿من السماوات والأرض﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رزقًا﴾, or attached to ﴿رزقًا﴾.
﴿شيئا ولا يستطيعون﴾: شيئًا is a mafʿūl bihi of ﴿رزقًا﴾, or a badal (substitute) from it in the sense of "a little"; the clause ﴿ولا يستطيعون﴾ is conjoined to the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position, or is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the wāw refers back to ﴿ما﴾, and what is meant by it is their gods.

muyesser-irab:74-74.t:
﴿فلا تضربوا لله الأمثال﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لا﴾ is prohibitive; ﴿تضربوا﴾ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تضربوا﴾; and الأمثال is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إن الله يعلم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the Divine Name its noun (ism), and the clause يعلم a khabar (predicate); the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya).
﴿وأنتم لا تعلمون﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause لا تعلمون a khabar.

muyesser-irab:75-75.t:
﴿ضرب الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; ﴿ضرب الله مثلًا﴾ is a verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿عبدًا﴾ is a badal (substitute) from ﴿مثلًا﴾; مملوكًا is a naʿt (adjective); the clause ﴿لا يقدر على شيء﴾ is a second naʿt; and ﴿على شيء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقدر﴾, i.e. of the dispositions [of affairs].
﴿ومن رزقناه منا رزقا حسنا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and من is conjoined to ﴿عبدًا مملوكًا﴾; ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, as though it were said: "and a free man whom We provided", to correspond with عبدًا; the clause ﴿رزقناه﴾ is a ṣila (relative clause) on the first [view], with no grammatical position, and a naʿt on the second; نا is the fāʿil and the hāʾ a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿منا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿رزقناه﴾; رزقًا is a second mafʿūl bihi, or an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and حسنًا is a naʿt of ﴿رزقًا﴾.
﴿فهو ينفق منه سرا وجهرا هل يستوون﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause ينفق a khabar (predicate); ﴿منه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينفق﴾; ﴿سرا﴾ is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "a secret spending", or is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "keeping it secret". ﴿جهرا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿سرا﴾, accusative. ﴿هل﴾ is an interrogative particle for negation. ﴿يستوون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the presence of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون﴾: الحمد is a mubtadaʾ; ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar; بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿لا يعلمون﴾ a khabar.

muyesser-irab:76-76.t:
﴿وضرب الله مثلا رجلين﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿ضرب الله مثلًا﴾ is a verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and رجلين is a badal (substitute) from ﴿مثلًا﴾.
﴿أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء﴾: ﴿أحدهما﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ﴿أبكم﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿لا يقدر على شيء﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أبكم﴾.
﴿وهو كلٌّ على مولاه﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and ﴿كلٌّ﴾ its khabar; ﴿على مولاه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كلٌّ﴾.
﴿أينما يوجهه لا يأت بخير﴾: أينما is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and it has been said: to its apodosis; لا is negating; ﴿يأت﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and ﴿بخير﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يأت﴾.
﴿هل يستوي هو ومن يأمر بالعدل وهو على صراط مستقيم﴾: ﴿هل﴾ is an interrogative particle whose meaning is negation; يستوي is an imperfect verb; ﴿هو﴾ is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) fāʿil; ﴿مَن﴾ is conjoined to the latent fāʿil in ﴿يستوي﴾; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, and ﴿على صراط مستقيم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted khabar; and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source does not parse يأمر بالعدل, which is the actual ṣila of مَن; the nominal clause وهو على صراط مستقيم would more usually be read as a ḥāl.]

muyesser-irab:77-77.t:
﴿ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وما أمر الساعة إلا كلمح البصر أو هو أقرب﴾: the wāw is resumptive; ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); غيب السماوات والأرض is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿ولله غيب السماوات والأرض﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿ما﴾ is negating; أمر is a mubtadaʾ and الساعة muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿كلمح البصر﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as khabar; ﴿لمح﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and ﴿البصر﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿أو﴾ is a conjunction; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and أقرب its khabar.
﴿إن الله على كل شيء قدير﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh) and the Divine Name its noun (ism); ﴿على كل شيء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قدير﴾; and قدير is the khabar of inna.

muyesser-irab:78-78.t:
﴿والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم﴾: ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause أخرجكم a khabar (predicate); ﴿من بطون أمهاتكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أخرجكم﴾.
﴿لا تعلمون شيئا﴾: the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf, i.e. "not knowing anything"; ﴿شيئًا﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة لعلكم تشكرون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; جعل is conjoined to أخرجكم, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa"; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second object of جعل; السمع is its first object, and الأبصار and الأفئدة are conjoined to it; لعل is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the kāf its noun (ism), and the clause تشكرون its khabar.

muyesser-irab:79-79.t:
﴿ألم يروا إلى الطير مسخرات في جو السماء﴾: the hamza is for interrogation of affirmation (taqrīr); لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; يروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿إلى الطير﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يروا﴾; مسخرات is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿في جو السماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مسخرات﴾.
﴿ما يمسكهن إلا الله﴾: the clause is circumstantial; ما is negating; يمسكهن is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿الله﴾ is the fāʿil. [Translator's note: the source states both a latent fāʿil and الله as fāʿil; as written.]
﴿إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون﴾: inna and its fronted khabar (predicate); the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات is its postponed noun (ism); ﴿لقوم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿آيات﴾; and the clause يؤمنون is a naʿt of قوم.

muyesser-irab:80-80.t:
﴿والله جعل لكم من بيوتكم سكنا﴾: ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause ﴿جعل﴾ a khabar (predicate); its first object is ﴿سكنًا﴾; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted first object [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "second object" is meant, since سكنًا has just been called the first]; ﴿من بيوتكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سكنًا﴾ and came before it. If ﴿جعل﴾ means "created", one of the two prepositional phrases is attached to it, and it is content with a single object.
﴿وجعل لكم من جلود الأنعام بيوتا تستخفونها يوم ظعنكم ويوم إقامتكم﴾: ﴿وجعل لكم من جلود الأنعام بيوتًا﴾ is conjoined to what preceded; the clause تستخفونها is a naʿt of ﴿بيوتًا﴾; in ﴿يوم ظعنكم﴾ the adverb is attached to ﴿تستخفونها﴾; and ﴿يوم إقامتكم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يوم ظعنكم﴾.
﴿ومن أصوافها وأوبارها وأشعارها أثاثا ومتاعا إلى حين﴾: ﴿ومن أصوافها﴾ is conjoined to ﴿من جلود الأنعام﴾; ﴿أثاثًا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿بيوتًا﴾, i.e. "and He made for you from their wool furnishings"; ﴿متاعًا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أثاثًا﴾; and ﴿إلى حين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿متاعًا﴾, or a naʿt of it.

muyesser-irab:81-81.t:
﴿والله جعل لكم مما خلق ظلالا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause ﴿جعل﴾ a khabar (predicate); ﴿ظلالًا﴾ is its first object; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object, a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Translator's note: so in the source, «مفعول ثان حال»]; مما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from ﴿ظلالا﴾. If ﴿جعل﴾ means "created", one of the two prepositional phrases is attached to it, and it is content with a single object. The clause ﴿خلق﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, with no grammatical position.
﴿وجعل لكم من الجبال أكنانا﴾: conjoined to what preceded.
﴿وجعل لكم سرابيل تقيكم الحر﴾: the clause ﴿تقيكم الحر﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سرابيل﴾; the conjoined item has been omitted because it is known, i.e. "and the cold".
﴿وسرابيل تقيكم بأسكم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; سرابيل is conjoined to the first سرابيل; the clause ﴿تقيكم﴾ is a naʿt; تقيكم is an imperfect verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); the kāf is its first object, and بأسكم its second object.
﴿كذلك يتم نعمته عليكم لعلكم تسلمون﴾: ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿يتم نعمته﴾ is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لعل is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the kāf its noun (ism), and the clause تسلمون its khabar.

muyesser-irab:82-82.t: ﴿فإن تولوا فإنما عليك البلاغ المبين﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; تولوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of in is omitted, i.e. "then there is no blame upon you"; the fāʾ gives the reason; ﴿إنما﴾ is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), inna restrained by the restraining mā (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ﴿عليك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿البلاغ﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and المبين a naʿt (adjective); and the clause ﴿فإن تولوا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:83-83.t: ﴿يعرفون نعمت الله ثم ينكرونها وأكثرهم الكافرون﴾: يعرفون is an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); نعمة الله is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿ثم﴾ is a conjunction for delay; ﴿ينكرونها﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يعرفون﴾; ﴿وأكثرهم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and الكافرون its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:84-84.t:
﴿ويوم نبعث من كل أمة شهيدا﴾: ﴿يوم﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember (udhkur)"; the clause ﴿نبعث﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); من كل أمة is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿شهيدًا﴾; and شهيدًا is a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ثم لا يؤذن للذين كفروا ولا هم يستعتبون﴾: ثم is a conjunction for delay; لا is negating; يؤذن is an imperfect verb in the passive (built for what has not had its agent named); للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) it; ولا: the wāw is conjunctive and لا negating; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يستعتبون a khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:85-85.t:
﴿وإذا رأى الذين ظلموا العذاب﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; إذا is a future adverb of time containing the sense of condition; the clause رأى is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); الذين is the fāʿil (agent) of رأى; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; and العذاب is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فلا يخفف عنهم ولا هم ينظرون﴾: the fāʾ links the answer of idhā; لا is negating; يخفف is an imperfect verb in the passive (built for what has not had its agent named), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), i.e. the punishment; لا is conjunctive [Translator's note: so in the source]; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ينظرون a khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: the source does not parse عنهم.]

muyesser-irab:86-86.t:
﴿وإذا رأى الذين أشركوا شركاءهم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; إذا is a future adverb of time containing the sense of condition; the clause رأى is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); الذين is the fāʿil (agent) of رأى; the clause أشركوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; and شركاءهم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of رأى.
﴿قالوا ربنا هؤلاء شركاؤنا الذين كنا ندعو من دونك﴾: the clause ﴿قالوا﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of ﴿إذا﴾; ﴿ربنا﴾ is a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf), the vocative particle having been omitted from it; ﴿هؤلاء﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and شركاؤنا a khabar (predicate); ﴿الذين﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿شركاؤنا﴾; ﴿كنا﴾ is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, ﴿نا﴾ its noun (ism), and the clause ﴿ندعو﴾ the khabar of ﴿كنا﴾; the clause ﴿كنا﴾ is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; and ﴿من دونك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted object of ندعو, i.e. "we call upon them and worship them besides You".
﴿فألقوا إليهم القول إنكم لكاذبون﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; ألقوا is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿إليهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ألقوا﴾; ﴿القول﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إنكم لكاذبون﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the kāf its noun, the lām the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and كاذبون its khabar; and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:87-87.t:
﴿وألقوا إلى الله يومئذ السلم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ألقوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and they are the disbelievers; ﴿إلى الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ألقوا﴾; ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم is an adverb of time attached to ﴿ألقوا﴾, and إذٍ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn, because the place [of the sukūn] is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the tanwīn compensating for an omitted clause; and السلم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ضل is a past verb; ﴿عنهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it; ﴿ما﴾ is the fāʿil of ضل; كانوا is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, the wāw its noun (ism), and the clause يفترون the khabar (predicate) of ﴿كانوا﴾; and the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:88-88.t: ﴿الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله زدناهم عذابا فوق العذاب بما كانوا يفسدون﴾: الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the clause ﴿زدناهم﴾; the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; ﴿صدوا عن سبيل الله﴾ is conjoined to ﴿كفروا﴾; ﴿زدناهم﴾ is a verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿عذابًا﴾ is a second object; ﴿فوق العذاب﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عذابًا﴾; ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿زدناهم﴾; the bāʾ is causal and ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. "because of their obstructing and their corrupting"; كانوا is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, the wāw its noun (ism), and the clause يفسدون its khabar.

muyesser-irab:89-89.t:
﴿ويوم نبعث في كل أمة شهيدا عليهم من أنفسهم﴾: ﴿يوم﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember (udhkur)"; the clause ﴿نبعث﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿في كل أمة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نبعث﴾; شهيدًا is a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿عليهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿شهيدًا﴾; and ﴿من أنفسهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿شهيدًا﴾.
﴿وجئنا بك شهيدا على هؤلاء﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; جئنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿جئنا﴾; ﴿شهيدًا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿على هؤلاء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿شهيدًا﴾.
﴿ونزلنا عليك الكتاب تبيانا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة وبشرى للمسلمين﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; نزلنا is conjoined to ﴿جئنا﴾, and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿عليك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نزلنا﴾; ﴿الكتاب﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿تبيانًا﴾ is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a ḥāl, i.e. "making clear"; ﴿لكل شيء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تبيانًا﴾; هدى, رحمة and بشرى are conjoined to ﴿تبيانًا﴾; and ﴿للمسلمين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿بشرى﴾.

muyesser-irab:90-90.t:
﴿إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the Divine Name its noun (ism), and the clause ﴿يأمر﴾ the khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿بالعدل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يأمر﴾; الإحسان is conjoined to العدل, and likewise ﴿إيتاء﴾; and ﴿ذي القربى﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي يعظكم لعلكم تذكرون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ينهى is conjoined to يأمر, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿عن الفحشاء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينهى﴾, and what follows it is conjoined to it; the clause ﴿يعظكم﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of يأمر and ينهى; لعل is an abrogating particle, the kāf its noun, and the clause ﴿تذكرون﴾ its khabar.

muyesser-irab:91-91.t:
﴿وأوفوا بعهد الله إذا عاهدتم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; أوفوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بعهد الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أوفوا﴾; إذا is a future adverb of time containing the sense of condition; and the clause عاهدتم is that to which the adverb is annexed (muḍāf ilayhi).
﴿ولا تنقضوا الأيمان بعد توكيدها وقد جعلتم الله عليكم كفيلا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تنقضوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā, and the wāw is the fāʿil; الأيمان is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿بعد﴾ is an adverb attached to ﴿تنقضوا﴾, and ﴿توكيدها﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of تنقضوا; قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); ﴿جعلتم الله﴾ is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; ﴿عليكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿كفيلًا﴾; and كفيلًا is the second object of جعلتم.
﴿إن الله يعلم ما تفعلون﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the Divine Name its noun (ism), and the clause ﴿يعلم...﴾ the khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿ما﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi, and تفعلون is its ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:92-92.t:
﴿ولا تكونوا كالتي نقضت غزلها من بعد قوة أنكاثا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تكونوا is an incomplete, abrogating past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; تكونوا is an imperfect verb], jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and the wāw is its noun (ism); ﴿كالتي﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of تكونوا, and ﴿التي﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿نقضت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position; غزلها is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿من بعد قوة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of نقضت, i.e. "having made it firm", or from its object, i.e. "made firm"; ﴿أنكاثًا﴾ is accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, i.e. "and so she made it into broken strands", or by ﴿نقضت﴾ containing the meaning of "made into (ṣayyarat)", so that it is a second object; it has been said: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of نقضت is "unravelled (nakathat)"; and it has been said: it is a ḥāl from ﴿غزلها﴾, i.e. "undone".
﴿تتخذون أيمانكم دخلا بينكم أن تكون أمة هي أربى من أمة﴾: the clause ﴿تتخذون﴾ is a ḥāl from the pronoun of تكونوا, i.e. "do not be like her, taking your oaths as deception"; ﴿تتخذون﴾ is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; أيمانكم is a first object, and ﴿دخلًا﴾ a second object; ﴿بينكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿دخلًا﴾; the interpreted maṣdar formed from ﴿أن﴾ and what falls within its scope is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for fear that there be"; تكون is an incomplete, abrogating past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; تكون is an imperfect verb]; ﴿أمة﴾ is the noun of تكون; ﴿هي﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ﴿أربى﴾ a khabar, and the clause is the khabar of تكون; and ﴿من أمة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أربى﴾.
﴿إنما يبلوكم الله به﴾: إنما is inna restrained by the restraining mā (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and it is for restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿يبلوكم الله﴾ is a verb, a fronted object and a postponed fāʿil; and ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يبلوكم﴾.
﴿وليبينن لكم يوم القيامة ما كنتم فيه تختلفون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; the lām occurs in the answer of an implied (muqaddar) oath; ﴿يبينن﴾ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, necessarily; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يبينن﴾; ﴿يوم القيامة﴾ is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿ما﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿كنتم﴾ is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; the clause كنتم is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿فيه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تختلفون﴾; and the clause ﴿تختلفون﴾ is the khabar of كنتم.

muyesser-irab:93-93.t:
﴿ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لو is conditional; ﴿شاء الله﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the lām occurs in the answer of law; ﴿جعلكم﴾ is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a first object; أمة is a second object, and واحدة a naʿt (adjective).
﴿ولكن يضل من يشاء﴾: the wāw is circumstantial [Translator's note: so in the source]; لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative because it has been lightened; ﴿يضل﴾ is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "huwa"; ﴿من﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); يشاء is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position; and ﴿يهدي من يشاء﴾ is conjoined to what preceded.
﴿ولتسألن عما كنتم تعملون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; the lām occurs in the answer of an implied (muqaddar) oath; تسألن is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), because the nūn [of emphasis] is not directly attached to it, so it is declinable (muʿrab), and the sign of its nominative is the presence of the nūn, which has been elided because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw, elided because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; ﴿عما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تسألن﴾; and the clause ﴿تعملون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم.

muyesser-irab:94-94.t:
﴿ولا تتخذوا أيمانكم دخلا بينكم﴾: لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); أيمانكم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ﴿دخلًا﴾ a second object; and ﴿بينكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿دخلًا﴾.
﴿فتزل قدم بعد ثبوتها﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation preceded by a prohibition; ﴿تزل﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an; ﴿قدم﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿بعد﴾ is an adverb attached to ﴿تزل﴾, and ثبوتها is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وتذوقوا السوء بما صددتم عن سبيل الله ولكم عذاب عظيم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; تذوقوا is conjoined to تزل; السوء is a mafʿūl bihi; the bāʾ is a preposition of causation, and ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and together with what it governs it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ﴿تذوقوا﴾; ﴿عن سبيل الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿صددتم﴾; ﴿لكم﴾ is a fronted khabar (predicate), عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and عظيم its naʿt.

muyesser-irab:95-95.t:
﴿ولا تشتروا بعهد الله ثمنا قليلا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تشتروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā; ﴿بعهد الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تشتروا﴾, the bāʾ entering upon what is given up; ﴿ثمنًا﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ﴿قليلًا﴾ a naʿt (adjective).
﴿إنما عند الله هو خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh) and ﴿ما﴾ its noun (ism); the adverb is attached to something omitted that is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير a khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of inna; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it; إن is conditional; كنتم is an incomplete, abrogating past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is the noun of kāna, and the clause تعلمون its khabar; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then do not break [them]".

muyesser-irab:96-96.t:
﴿ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق﴾: ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عندكم﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause), and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; the clause ينفد is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿ما﴾; ﴿وما عند الله باق﴾ is conjoined to what came before and is like it in its i'rab.
﴿ولنجزين الذين صبروا أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون﴾: the lām occurs in the answer of an implied (muqaddar) oath; نجزين is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is made emphatic by the doubled nūn, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu"; ﴿الذين صبروا﴾ is its object, and أجرهم a second object of ﴿نجزين﴾; ﴿بأحسن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نجزين﴾; ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); كانوا is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, the wāw its noun (ism), and the clause يعملون its khabar. It has been said: ﴿ما﴾ is a relative, the implied meaning being: "with a recompense better than their deeds which they used to do in this world", or "We make the reward proportionate to the best of their deeds".

muyesser-irab:97-97.t:
﴿من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى﴾: من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عمل﴾ is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); صالحا: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿عمل﴾, or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "does a righteous deed". ﴿من ذكر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿عمل﴾; ﴿أو﴾ is a conjunction; and ﴿أنثى﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ذكر﴾.
﴿وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and ﴿مؤمن﴾ a khabar (predicate), and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿فلنحيينه﴾: the fāʾ is linking, the lām occurs in the answer of an implied (muqaddar) oath, ﴿نحيينه﴾ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿حياة﴾ is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq, because it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar). ﴿طيبة﴾ is a naʿt (adjective). The clause ﴿فلنحيينه﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of ﴿من﴾. It has been said: ﴿من﴾ is a relative noun, and the fāʾ enters because of the scent of condition in the qualified noun [Translator's note: so in the source, «الموصوف»; presumably "the relative (al-mawṣūl)" is meant], and the clause ﴿فلنحيينه﴾ is its khabar.
﴿ولنجزينهم أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون﴾: the lām occurs in the answer of the oath; نجزينهم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is made emphatic by the doubled nūn, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu"; ﴿هم﴾ is its object, and ﴿أجرهم﴾ a second object of ﴿نجزين﴾; ﴿بأحسن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نجزين﴾; ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya; كانوا is an incomplete, abrogating past verb, the wāw its noun (ism), and the clause يعملون its khabar. It has been said: ما is a relative, the implied meaning being: "with a recompense better than their deeds which they used to do in this world", or "We make the reward proportionate to the best of their deeds".

muyesser-irab:98-98.t: ﴿فإذا قرأت القرآن فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; إذا is an adverb for future time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿استعذ﴾; the clause ﴿قرأت﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); القرآن is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "when you intend to recite the Qur'an"; the fāʾ links the answer; استعذ is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; ﴿بالله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿استعذ﴾; ﴿من الشيطان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, likewise attached to ﴿استعذ﴾; and الرجيم is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:99-99.t: ﴿إنه ليس له سلطان على الذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون﴾: the clause gives the reason for the command; إن is an abrogating particle (nāsikh), the hāʾ its noun (ism), and the clause ﴿ليس﴾ its khabar (predicate); ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar of ﴿ليس﴾, and ﴿سلطان﴾ is its postponed noun; ﴿على الذين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿سلطان﴾; آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; and ﴿على ربهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يتوكلون﴾.

muyesser-irab:100-100.t: ﴿إنما سلطانه على الذين يتولونه والذين هم به مشركون﴾: ﴿إنما﴾ is inna restrained by the restraining mā (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ﴿سلطانه﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿على الذين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿يتولونه﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, with no grammatical position; ﴿الذين﴾ is conjoined to the first ﴿الذين﴾; ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مشركون﴾; ﴿مشركون﴾ is the khabar of ﴿هم﴾; and the clause ﴿هم به مشركون﴾ is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:101-101.t:
﴿وإذا بدلنا آية مكان آية﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; إذا is a future adverb of time; ﴿بدلنا﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿آية﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مكان﴾ is a second object of ﴿بدلنا﴾, or an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بدلنا﴾; and ﴿آية﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿والله أعلم بما ينزل قالوا﴾: the wāw is parenthetical, and the clause is parenthetical between the condition of ﴿إذا﴾ and its answer, with no grammatical position; ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ﴿أعلم﴾ a khabar (predicate); ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعلم﴾; ﴿ينزل﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿قالوا﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of ﴿إذا﴾.
﴿إنما أنت مفتر بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون﴾: the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); إنما is inna restrained by the restraining mā (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ﴿أنت﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and ﴿مفتر﴾ a khabar; ﴿بل﴾ is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿أكثرهم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿لا يعلمون﴾ a khabar; the object of يعلمون has been omitted because it is known, i.e. "the reality of substitution and abrogation and their benefit".

muyesser-irab:102-102.t:
