muyesser-irab:54-54.t: ﴿ثم إذا كشف الضر عنكم إذا فريق منكم بربهم يشركون﴾: ثم is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, its implied form being "some of you associate partners" (أشرك بعضكم); the clause ﴿كشف﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); الضر is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿عنكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿كشف﴾; إذا is [the إذا] of surprise (fujāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; فريق is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿بربهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يشركون﴾; and the clause يشركون is the khabar (predicate) of فريق.

muyesser-irab:55-55.t:
﴿ليكفروا بما آتيناهم فتمتعوا﴾: ﴿ليكفروا﴾: the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl); يكفروا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿يشركون﴾, i.e. "their associating partners is caused by their disbelief in their Lord". It is also said that the lām is the lām of becoming (ṣayrūra) or of consequence (ʿāqiba), i.e. "the consequence of their associating others with Allah is their ingratitude for the blessing, which is the removal of harm from them"; and the preposition and its genitive noun — consisting of the lām and the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and the verb in ﴿ليكفروا﴾ — are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يكفروا﴾; the clause آتيناهم is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; and ﴿فتمتعوا﴾ is a clause governed by an omitted saying, i.e. "say to them, O Muhammad: enjoy yourselves".
﴿فسوف تعلمون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; سوف is a particle of futurity; ﴿تعلمون﴾ is a verb and fāʿil (agent); and its object is omitted, its implied form being "the outcome of that".

nahhas-irab:103-103.t:
Al-Ḥasan read إِنَّما يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ لِسانُ الَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ, with «بشر» without tanwīn (nunation) and «اللسان» with the definite article, اللسان being nominative. «بشر» is nominative (marfūʿ) by its verb, and «اللسان» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «أعجميّ». The tanwīn was dropped from «بشر» because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and Sībawayh cited:
[al-Mutaqārib] 264-
ولا ذاكر الله إلّا قليلا
(Gloss: "…nor remembering Allah except a little" — with ذاكر left without tanwīn before الله.)
Similar to it is the reading of whoever read قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 2], and likewise وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سابِقُ النَّهارِ [Yā Sīn: 20] with النهار in the accusative. «[Translator's note: the verse is Yā Sīn 36:40, not 20, as printed in the source.]» The people of Medina «[Translator's note: the source has «أقل المدينة», evidently a misprint for «أهل المدينة».]» and the people of Basra read يُلْحِدُونَ with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ, and the Kufans read يلحدون with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ḥāʾ. The more eloquent usage is «يلحدون»; from it one says: رجل ملحد, i.e. a man inclining away from the truth. This is made clear by وَمَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحادٍ [al-Ḥajj: 25], for this is from ألحد يلحد and nothing else. One says: لحدت القبر, i.e. I made a niche (laḥd) in it, and ألحدت الميّت, i.e. I put the dead man in the niche.
وَهذا لِسانٌ: it is said that it means the Qurʾan; it called it a "tongue" by extension of usage, just as one says "So-and-so speaks with the tongue of the Arabs", i.e. in their language. Likewise اللسان الذي يلحدون إليه means his speech; on this basis a message is called a "tongue", as the poet said: [al-Wāfir] 265-
لسان السّوء تهديها إلينا
(Gloss: "an evil tongue [i.e. an evil message] that you send to us".)

nahhas-irab:106-106.t:
مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمانِهِ: مَنْ is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for «الكاذبين».
إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ is in the position of the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā) in an exception. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: except one who is coerced.
Such a person may say what outwardly is a lie and disbelief while not believing it; but he may not tell an outright lie in any way. Rather he says "So-and-so is a liar" meaning "according to their claim", or he means by it someone other than the Prophet ﷺ who really is a liar; for lying is foul, and it is not possible that Allah should permit it in any circumstance. The proof of its foulness is that the one who utters it is not trusted in what he reports.
وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالْإِيمانِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and it is an explanation of what came before. مَنْ شَرَحَ بِالْكُفْرِ is a mubtadaʾ. فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ is in the position of the khabar.

nahhas-irab:107-107.t: اسْتَحَبُّوا الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا عَلَى الْآخِرَةِ: al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: لا جَرَمَ is only ever a reply. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: مِنْ بَعْدِها, i.e. after the trial (fitna).

nahhas-irab:111-111.t: يَوْمَ تَأْتِي is in the position of the accusative, i.e. Forgiving, Merciful on the day every soul comes; and it may have the meaning: and remember the day every soul comes.

nahhas-irab:112-112.t: وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا قَرْيَةً, i.e. the likeness of a town. فَكَفَرَتْ بِأَنْعُمِ اللَّهِ: أنعم is the plural of نعمة according to Sībawayh; Quṭrub said: it is the plural of نعم, like ودّ and أدود.

nahhas-irab:116-116.t: وَلا تَقُولُوا لِما تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ: الكذب is accusative, with the meaning "because of your tongues' describing the lie". And he said: الكذب — he throws the vowel of the dāl onto the kāf. «[Translator's note: the text here is as printed; it apparently refers to a reading الكِذْب, with the vowel of the dhāl transferred to the kāf.]» The people of Syria, or some of them, read وَلا تَقُولُوا لِما تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ as a naʿt (adjective) of the tongues «[Translator's note: i.e. the reading الكُذُبُ in the nominative, qualifying ألسنتكم; the source prints the ordinary vowelling.]», and al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Ṭalḥa and Abū Maʿmar read لِما تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ in the genitive, as a naʿt of ما or a badal (substitute) for it. «[Translator's note: i.e. the reading الكَذِبِ in the genitive; the source prints the ordinary vowelling.]»

nahhas-irab:117-117.t: مَتاعٌ قَلِيلٌ: on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. their enjoyment in this world is a little enjoyment, i.e. the length of their remaining. Outside the Qurʾan متاعا would be permissible as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. they are given enjoyment (يمتعون متاعا).

nahhas-irab:120-120.t: كانَ أُمَّةً: the khabar (predicate) of kāna. قانِتاً: a naʿt (adjective) or a second khabar. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned وَلَمْ يَكُ in more than one place.

nahhas-irab:124-124.t: إِنَّما جُعِلَ السَّبْتُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ: some of them said: we do not want Friday, and some of them said: we do not want the Sabbath; so rest on the day of the Sabbath was made obligatory upon them.

nahhas-irab:127-127.t:
وَلا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ: it is said that the meaning is: do not grieve over the unbelievers, for your duty is only to call them to faith; and it is said that the meaning is: do not grieve over the martyrs, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has rewarded them — among them was Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, may Allah be pleased with him, and concerning him was revealed وَإِنْ عاقَبْتُمْ فَعاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ ما عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ [al-Naḥl: 126]. وَلا تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ refers to the unbelievers; no one said otherwise. Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām reported that Nāfiʿ read وَلا تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ with kasra on the ḍād. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is not known from Nāfiʿ. The Kufans — al-Farrāʾ and others — said: «الضيق» with fatḥa on the ḍād is in the heart and the breast, and «الضيق» with kasra on the ḍād is in a garment, a house and the like of what is seen. Al-Farrāʾ said: if you see الضيق with fatḥa on the ḍād occurring in the place of الضّيق, it is a lightened form of ضيّق or the plural of ضيقة. The Basrans know nothing of this distinction; they said: if you mean the maṣdar (verbal noun) you say الضيق, as you say البيع, and if you mean the noun you say الضيق, as you say العلم; and they permitted lightening ضيّق.

nahhas-irab:128-128.t: إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا: الَّذِينَ is genitive through مع being annexed to it, because مع according to al-Khalīl is a noun when you give the ʿayn a fatḥa, and if you make it quiescent it is a particle. وَالَّذِينَ: conjoined (maʿṭūf). هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), within the ṣila (relative clause).

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Naḥl (The Bee)
Meccan, except for three verses at its end, for they were revealed between Mecca and Medina.
﷽
His words, Exalted is He: ﴿أتى أمْرُ اللَّهِ فَلا تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ﴾: "أمر الله" (the command of Allah) is the various kinds of punishment that Allah promised them as requital for their disbelief. The proof of this is His words: ﴿حَتّى إذا جاءَ أمْرُنا وفارَ التَّنُّورُ﴾ [Hūd: 40], that is: what We had promised them came; and likewise His words: ﴿أتاها أمْرُنا لَيْلا أوْ نَهارًا فَجَعَلْناها حَصِيدًا﴾ [Yūnus: 24]. That is because they sought to hasten the punishment and thought the matter of the Hour slow in coming, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that it, in its nearness, is as something that has already come, as He said: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ [al-Qamar: 1], and as He said: ﴿وَما أمْرُ السّاعَةِ إلا كَلَمْحِ البَصَرِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 77].

His words: ﴿سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: its meaning is: His being declared free of all evil. This is how it has come in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ, and this is how the authorities on the language explained it; they said: its meaning is declaring Allah free of evil, and Allah's being clear of evil. The poet said:
؎أقُولُ لِما جاءَ في فَخْرِهِ سُبْحانَ مِن عَلْقَمَةَ الفاجِرِ
(I say, when his boasting reached me: "subḥāna" from ʿAlqama the wicked!)
that is: [I declare] clearness from him.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
His words: ﴿مِنهُ شَرابٌ ومِنهُ شَجَرٌ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾: the meaning is that it makes grow the shrubs (الشجر) which the camels graze; everything that grows on the earth is "شجر". The poet said, describing horses:
؎نَعْلُفُها اللَّحْمَ إذا عَزَّ الشَّجَرْ والخَيْلُ في إطْعامِها اللَّحْمَ ضَرَرْ
(We feed them "meat" when vegetation is scarce, and for horses there is harm in feeding them meat.)
He means that they give the horses milk to drink when the land is barren.

His words: ﴿فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾, that is: you pasture [your herds]. One says "أسَمْتُ الإبل" when you have pastured the camels, and "قد سامت، تسوم، وهي سائمة" when they have grazed. That is taken from "السُّومة", which is a mark; its interpretation is that by their grazing they leave marks on the land.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His words: ﴿وَتَرى الفُلْكَ مَواخِرَ فِيهِ﴾: the meaning of "مواخر فيه" is: running, sailing along and cleaving the water.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿وَألْقى في الأرْضِ رَواسِيَ أنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ﴾: "رواسي" means firm mountains, fixed. "أن تميد": its meaning is: lest it sway (كراهة أن تميد). The meaning of "تميد" is: it does not stay still. One says "ماد الرجلُ يميد ميدًا" when he feels dizzy (as if turned about), and "المَيْدى" are those who become dizzy when they ride on the sea. "أن تميد" is in the position of the accusative (fī mawḍiʿ naṣb), a mafʿūl lahā (object of purpose) [Translator's note: so in the text, i.e. mafʿūl lahu]. ﴿وَأنْهارًا وسُبُلا﴾: the meaning is: and He placed in it firm mountains, rivers and ways, because the meaning of "ألقى في الأرض رواسي" is: He placed in it firm mountains; the proof of this is His words: ﴿والجِبالَ أوْتادًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 7].

zajjaj:16-16.t: His words: ﴿وَبِالنَّجْمِ هم يَهْتَدُونَ﴾: "النجم" (the star) and "النجوم" (the stars) have one meaning, just as you say "كثر الدرهمُ في أيدي الناس" (the dirham has become plentiful in people's hands) and "كثرت الدراهمُ" (the dirhams have become plentiful). Allah, exalted be His praise, created the stars for several things: among them, that they were made an adornment for the lowest heaven; among them, that they were made missiles against the devils; among them, that people are guided by them; and among them, that the number of years and reckoning are known by them.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His words: ﴿يُنَـزِّلُ المَلائِكَةَ بِالرُّوحِ مِن أمْرِهِ﴾. It is also read: "تُنَزَّلُ الملائكةُ" (the angels are sent down). Several other forms are grammatically possible in it which I do not know to have been read: "يَنْزِلُ الملائكةُ", "يُنْزِلُ الملائكةَ" and "تَنَزَّلُ الملائكةُ". "بالروح": the Spirit (الروح) — and Allah knows best — is whatever of Allah's command contains life for souls, and guidance to Allah's command. The proof of this is His words: ﴿أنْ أنْذِرُوا أنَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلا أنا فاتَّقُونِ﴾; the meaning is: warn the people of disbelief and disobedience that there is no god but Me, that is: command them to affirm My oneness and not to associate anything with Me.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾; it is also read "تدعون من دون الله", with tāʾ and with yāʾ. ﴿لا يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْئًا وهم يُخْلَقُونَ﴾: by this are meant the idols which the Arabs used to worship.

zajjaj:21-21.t:
﴿أمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أحْياءٍ﴾, that is: and they are dead, not living.

His words: ﴿وَما يَشْعُرُونَ أيّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾, that is: they do not perceive when they will be raised. "أيّان" is in the position of the accusative by His word "يُبعثون", but it is indeclinable (mabnī), without nunation, because it has the sense of the interrogative; so it does not take case inflection, just as "كم", "متى", "كيف" and "أين" do not take case inflection — except that the nūn was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

If someone asks: why was it not given kasra? It is said: the preferred choice, when there is an alif before the last quiescent letter, is to give it fatḥa, because the fatḥa is more akin to the alif and lighter with it. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl held that if you apply tarkhīm (truncation in the vocative) to a man named "أسحارّ", you say: "يا أسحارَّ — with doubled rāʾ — أقبل" (O Asḥārr, come!), giving the rāʾ fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Likewise you choose fatḥa next to [a letter with] fatḥa: you say, when giving the imperative of غضّ (to lower): "غُضَّ يا هذا" (lower [your gaze], you!).

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His words: ﴿لا جَرَمَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما يُسِرُّونَ وما يُعْلِنُونَ﴾: the meaning of "لا جرم" is: it is true that Allah knows, and it is established.

As for "لا", it is a rejection of their deed. The poet said:
؎وَلَقَدْ طَعَنْتُ أبا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً جَرَمَتْ فَزارَةَ بَعْدَها أنْ يَغْضَبُوا
(I pierced Abū ʿUyayna with a thrust that, after it, made it due (جرمت) for Fazāra to be angry.)
The meaning is: it made Fazāra deserving of anger.

zajjaj:24-24.t: His words: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ لَهم ماذا أنْـزَلَ رَبُّكم قالُوا أساطِيرُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾: "ما" is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and "ذا" is in the position of "الذي" (which); the meaning is: "What is it that your Lord has sent down?" "أساطير" is nominative (marfūʿ) as the answer, as if they said: "What He sent down is the tales of the ancients", that is: the lies of the ancients; its singular is "أُسطورة".

zajjaj:3-3.t: Then He made known what of His creation points to His oneness, and said: ﴿خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ بِالحَقِّ تَعالى عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: He is exalted above those whom they associated with Him, because they create nothing while they themselves are created.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His words: ﴿خَلَقَ الإنْسانَ مِن نُطْفَةٍ فَإذا هو خَصِيمٌ مُبِينٌ﴾: He has abbreviated here, and He mentioned the changing states of man in more than one place in the Quran.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His words: ﴿والأنْعامَ خَلَقَها لَكم فِيها دِفْءٌ﴾: "الأنعام" is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmar) verb; the meaning is: "He created the livestock — He created them", [the overt "خلقها"] explaining the implied verb. "الدِّفء" is what keeps them warm from their camel hair and their wool. "الأنعام" is most often used specifically of camels, but it can apply to camels, sheep and cattle. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed us that in livestock there is what keeps us warm, and He did not say: "In them there is for you what shelters you and keeps you warm against the cold", because what shields from heat shields from cold, and what shields from cold shields from heat. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in another place: ﴿سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 81], and it is understood that they also protect from cold. Likewise, when it is said ﴿لَكم فِيها دِفْءٌ﴾, it is understood that they shield from cold and shield from heat.

His words: ﴿وَمَنافِعُ﴾, that is: and their benefits: their milk, their urine and other things. ﴿وَمِنها تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ ﴿وَلَكم فِيها جَمالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وحِينَ تَسْرَحُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 6]: "الإراحة" is the camels' returning in the evening from their pastures to the place where they stay. ﴿وَحِينَ تَسْرَحُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 6], that is: when you let them out to graze. In what a person owns there is beauty and adornment, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿المالُ والبَنُونَ زِينَةُ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾ [al-Kahf: 46]. Wealth (المال) is not restricted to silver and gold coin to the exclusion of other possessions; most of the wealth of the Arabs is camels, just as most of the wealth of the people of Basra is palm trees: they say "So-and-so's wealth is at such-and-such a place", meaning the palm trees.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His words: ﴿وَتَحْمِلُ أثْقالَكم إلى بَلَدٍ لَمْ تَكُونُوا بالِغِيهِ إلا بِشِقِّ الأنْفُسِ﴾: it is read with fatḥa and with kasra [i.e. بِشَقّ and بِشِقّ], that is: "If you had taken the trouble to reach it on something other than camels, that would have been hard for you."

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His words: ﴿والخَيْلَ والبِغالَ والحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوها﴾, that is: and He created horses, mules and donkeys for riding. Many people say that this verse indicates that the flesh of horses, mules and donkeys is forbidden, because He said about camels: ﴿وَمِنها تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 5], ﴿وَلِتَبْلُغُوا عَلَيْها حاجَةً في صُدُورِكُمْ﴾ [Ghāfir: 80]

while He said about horses: ﴿والخَيْلَ والبِغالَ والحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوها وزِينَةً﴾, and did not mention eating with regard to them. Some people said: if they had been made forbidden by this verse, the Prophet ﷺ would not have forbidden the flesh of domestic donkeys, and what the Quran indicated would have sufficed him. This is a mistake, because the Quran has indicated that wine is forbidden, and yet the Prophet ﷺ said: «"Wine itself has been forbidden"». So the Prophet ﷺ mentioned that what was forbidden in the Book is forbidden, as emphasis of it and additional clarification. "وزينةً" is accusative as a mafʿūl lahā (object of purpose) [Translator's note: so in the text, i.e. mafʿūl lahu]; the meaning is: "and He created them as adornment".

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His words: ﴿وَعَلى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ ومِنها جائِرٌ﴾, that is: upon Allah is making clear the straight road to Him by proofs and demonstrations.

His words: ﴿وَمِنها جائِرٌ﴾: "جائر", that is: among the ways there are roads that do not lead straight to the truth.

His words: ﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ لَهَداكم أجْمَعِينَ﴾, that is: had Allah willed, He would have sent down a sign that compels creation to believe in Him; but He, Mighty and Majestic, guides whom He wills and calls to a straight path.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His words: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا أوْزارَهم كامِلَةً يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ ومِن أوْزارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهم بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾: these people used to turn away whoever wanted to follow the Prophet ﷺ, and when they were asked about what he had brought they said: "What he has brought is the tales of the ancients." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that by this they bear the sins of those who disbelieved because of what they said, and that this does not diminish anything of the sin of the follower.

His words: ﴿ألا ساءَ ما يَزِرُونَ﴾: "ما" is in the position of the nominative (fī mawḍiʿ rafʿ), just as you put [a noun] in the nominative with "نعم" and "بئس". The meaning is: "Evil is the thing — their burden (ساء الشيءُ وزرُهم)"; this is as you say "بئس الشيء" (evil is the thing).

zajjaj:26-26.t: His words: ﴿قَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ فَأتى اللَّهُ بُنْيانَهم مِنَ القَواعِدِ﴾, that is: from the pillars of the building that support it. ﴿فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ مِن فَوْقِهِمْ﴾: it is related that this is in the story of Nimrod son of Canaan: he built a tower with which to plot, and its roof fell upon him and his companions. Some said: this is a parable: their deeds which they did were made like one who builds a building that falls on him; so the harm of their deeds is upon them like the harm to the builder when his building falls on him.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His words: ﴿وَيَقُولُ أيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ﴾; and "تُشاقُّونِ فيهم", with kasra on the nūn. We have explained the like of this. "شركائي" (My partners) is only a reporting of their own claim; Allah, exalted be His praise, has no partner. The meaning is: where are those who, in your claim, are My partners?

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿فَألْقَوُا السَّلَمَ ما كُنّا نَعْمَلُ مِن سُوءٍ﴾, that is: they offered submission. He mentioned "السَّلَم" — and "السلم" is peace — because He had mentioned opposition (المشاقّة); and peace stands over against opposition and enmity.

﴿ما كُنّا نَعْمَلُ مِن سُوءٍ﴾, that is: they said: "We were not doing any evil."

zajjaj:30-30.t:
﴿وَقِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا ماذا أنْـزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾: "ما" and "ذا" are like a single thing, and the meaning is: "What thing has your Lord sent down?" ﴿قالُوا خَيْرًا﴾ is [accusative] as the answer to "ماذا"; the meaning is: He sent down good. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أحْسَنُوا في هَذِهِ الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةٌ﴾: it is possible that these words were mentioned to show that by what they said they earned a good reward, and it is possible that it is an explanation of their saying "خيرًا". "حسنةٌ" in the nominative is the reading. "للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنةً" [in the accusative] is grammatically possible, but do not recite it that way; its possibility is that its meaning is that "He sent down good" — [that good] was made for those who did good in this world a good thing (حسنةً), that is: it was made for them a recompense in this world, before the Hereafter.

His words: ﴿وَلَدارُ الآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ ولَنِعْمَ دارُ المُتَّقِينَ﴾: the meaning is: "and excellent indeed is the abode of the God-fearing — the abode of the Hereafter". But what explains His words "دار المتقين" is His words: ﴿جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها﴾ [al-Naḥl: 31], which is nominative by an implied "هي" (it is); as if, when you said "ولنعم دار المتقين", in answer to one asking, that is: which abode is this praised one?, you said: "Gardens of Eden which they enter." If you wish, you may make it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the meaning would be: "Gardens of Eden — excellent is the abode of the God-fearing."

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His words: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا أنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ﴾, that is: to take their souls, or that what Allah promised them of His punishment should come.

His words: ﴿كَذَلِكَ فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ وما ظَلَمَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾, that is: thus they did, and Allah's command came upon them with punishment: ﴿فَأصابَهم سَيِّئاتُ ما عَمِلُوا﴾ [al-Naḥl: 34].

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His words: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ أشْرَكُوا لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما عَبَدْنا مِن دُونِهِ مِن شَيْءٍ نَحْنُ ولا آباؤُنا ولا حَرَّمْنا مِن دُونِهِ مِن شَيْءٍ كَذَلِكَ فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾: there is dispute over this verse and those like it, and the people of the Quran and the Sunna ought to establish the true explanation of it, because some people have claimed that whoever says this has disbelieved, and that whoever of the servants says that he does nothing except what Allah wills has disbelieved. This is a bad interpretation. Those people only disbelieved and lied because they used to say "Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him" by way of mockery.

The proof of this is that the people of Shuʿayb said to Shuʿayb: ﴿أصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا أوْ أنْ نَفْعَلَ في أمْوالِنا ما نَشاءُ إنَّكَ لأنْتَ الحَلِيمُ الرَّشِيدُ﴾ [Hūd: 87]; had they said this to him believing it, they would have been believers; they only said it mockingly.

The community has agreed that if Allah had willed that none other than He be worshipped, with a will that compels to that, no one would have been able to do otherwise; but Allah, exalted be His praise, has charged the servants with worship, granted success to whom He loved to grant success, and led astray whom He loved to lead astray. These people said this as confirming what was said to them, [while] they were deniers, since there is consensus that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is able to compel the servants to obey Him. Allah made known that they are deniers, just as those before them denied, and said: ﴿فَهَلْ عَلى الرُّسُلِ إلا البَلاغُ المُبِينُ﴾, that is: the conveying through which they make clear that they are prophets.

zajjaj:36-36.t: His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنا في كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولا أنِ اُعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ واجْتَنِبُوا الطّاغُوتَ﴾: Allah made known that He sent the messengers with the command to worship, while it [i.e. His decree] is behind the leading astray and the guidance. So He said: ﴿فَمِنهم مَن هَدى اللَّهُ ومِنهم مَن حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِ الضَّلالَةُ﴾; this shows that had they said that [i.e. "Had Allah willed…"] believing it, they would have been truthful. Then He confirmed that, saying: ﴿إنْ تَحْرِصْ عَلى هُداهم فَإنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَن يُضِلُّ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 37]. It has also been read: "فإن الله لا يُهدى من يُضِلّ" (whom Allah leads astray is not guided), as He said: ﴿مَن يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلا هادِيَ لَهُ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 186]. There is a third way of reading it: "لا يَهدي من يَضِلّ" (He does not guide whoever goes astray), and it is the least of the three.

zajjaj:38-38.t: His words: ﴿بَلى وعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا﴾: "وعدًا" is accusative (manṣūb), emphatic [i.e. an emphatic maṣdar]; the meaning is: "Yes indeed, Allah will raise them — a promise binding upon Him, true." ﴿لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ الَّذِي يَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 39]: this is of two kinds. It may be attached to the raising, the meaning being: "Yes indeed, Allah will raise them in order to make clear to them" ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أنَّهم كانُوا كاذِبِينَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 39]. Or it may be that "ليبين لهم الذي يختلفون فيه" is attached to His words: "And We have certainly sent to every community a messenger, to make clear to them their disagreement, and that before him they were in error."

zajjaj:40-40.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّما قَوْلُنا لِشَيْءٍ إذا أرَدْناهُ أنْ نَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾: the reading is the nominative (فيكونُ), and it has also been read in the accusative (فيكونَ). The nominative is on the basis of "فهو" (then it…), in the sense: "Whatever Allah wills, it comes to be." The accusative is of two kinds: one is that His word "فيكونَ" is conjoined to "أن نقول", [i.e.] "أن نقول فيكونَ"; and it may be accusative as the answer to "كن". "قولُنا" is nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is "أن نقول"; the meaning is: "Our word for every thing willed is only Our saying 'Be'." In this the servants are addressed with what they can comprehend; and whatever Allah wills comes to be in every case,

and in accordance with the speed He wills. Had He willed to create the world — the heavens and the earth — in the space of the blink of an eye, He would have been able to do so; but the servants were addressed with what they can comprehend. So Allah made known to them how easy for Him is the creation of things before they exist: He made known that whenever He wills a thing, it is, and that when He says "Be", it is — not that the thing existed before it was created; the meaning is only: when We will a thing, We say on account of it, "Be, O thing willed", and it comes to be, according to the measure of Allah's will. [This was said] because the people — I mean the idolaters — denied the resurrection, and swore by Allah their most solemn oaths that Allah would not raise up one who dies; that is the meaning of His words: ﴿وَكانُوا يُصِرُّونَ عَلى الحِنْثِ العَظِيمِ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 46], that is: they used to swear that they would not be raised.

It has come in the exegesis that al-ḥinth (the sin) is polytheism, because whoever believes this — let alone swears to it — is a polytheist. So He, Majestic and Exalted, said: ﴿بَلى وعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا﴾ [al-Naḥl: 38], that is: yes indeed, He will raise them — a promise binding upon Him, true. "حقًّا" is accusative, an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun), because when He says "He will raise them" this indicates "He promised the raising with a promise (وعد بالبعث وعدًا)". [Translator's note: the explanation given fits "وعدًا" rather than "حقًّا"; translated as written.]

zajjaj:41-41.t:
His words: ﴿والَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا في اللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ ما ظُلِمُوا لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهم في الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةً ولأجْرُ الآخِرَةِ أكْبَرُ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: these were people whom the idolaters used to torture for holding to faith; among them were Ṣuhayb and Bilāl. That was because Ṣuhayb said to the people of Mecca: "I am an old man; if I am with you I will not benefit you, and if I am against you I will not harm you. Take my wealth and let me go." So he gave them his wealth and emigrated to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said to him: "The sale has profited, O Ṣuhayb."

And ʿUmar said: "What an excellent man Ṣuhayb is! Had he not feared Allah, he would not have disobeyed Him." Its interpretation is: even if he were secure from His punishment and penalty, he would not abandon obedience nor incline to disobedience because of his being secure from punishment.

The meaning of ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهم في الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةً﴾ is: because they came to be with the Prophet ﷺ, entered Islam, and heard Allah's praise of them.

zajjaj:43-43.t: His words: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْنا مِن قَبْلِكَ إلا رِجالا نُوحِي﴾; also "يُوحى إليهم" (it is revealed to them) and "يُوحي إليهم" (He reveals to them). The first two readings are good, and the third is weak, because He mentioned "أرسلنا" (We sent); so for the wording to be "نوحي" (We reveal) or "يوحى" is better, because "نوحي" agrees with both wording and meaning, while "يوحى" is construed only according to the meaning, since the meaning is: "Allah sent none but men to whom revelation is given." This was said to them only because they said: "Why has an angel not been sent down to him, or a warner come with him?"

zajjaj:44-44.t:
So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that the messengers are human beings, except that revelation is given to them. Then He made known how the soundness of their prophethood is to be inferred, and said: ﴿بِالبَيِّناتِ والزُّبُرِ﴾, that is: with the signs and proofs. "الزُّبُر" are books; its singular is "زبور". One says "زبرتُ الكتاب" and "ذبرته" (I wrote the book) with one meaning. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
؎عَرَفْتُ الدِّيارَ كَرَقْمِ الدَّوا ةِ يَذْبُرُها الكاتِبُ الحِمْيَرِيُّ
(I recognised the abodes, like the lines of the inkwell that the Ḥimyarite scribe writes.)
His words: ﴿فاسْألُوا أهْلَ الذِّكْرِ إنْ كُنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 43]: there are two views on this. It was said: ask the people of the books, the people of the Torah and the Gospel — and the people of all the books acknowledge that the prophets were all human beings. It was also said: ﴿فاسْألُوا أهْلَ الذِّكْرِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 43], that is: ask those of the People of the Book who have believed. It is possible — and Allah knows best — that it was said to them: ask everyone who is known for knowledge, whether he agrees with the people of this religion or differs from them. The proof that "the people of the Reminder (أهل الذكر)" are the people of the books is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿وَأنْـزَلْنا إلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنّاسِ ما نُـزِّلَ إلَيْهِمْ﴾
and His words: ﴿وَهَذا ذِكْرٌ مُبارَكٌ أنْـزَلْناهُ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 50].

zajjaj:45-45.t: His words: ﴿أفَأمِنَ الَّذِينَ مَكَرُوا السَّيِّئاتِ أنْ يَخْسِفَ اللَّهُ بِهِمُ الأرْضَ﴾, that is: do they feel secure that He will not do to them what He did to the people of Lot and those of the past nations who were destroyed by the hastening of punishment in this world? ﴿أوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ العَذابُ مِن حَيْثُ لا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ is conjoined to "أن يخسف".

zajjaj:46-46.t: ﴿أوْ يَأْخُذَهم في تَقَلُّبِهِمْ﴾, that is: in their going about on their journeys and in all their other comings and goings.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
﴿أوْ يَأْخُذَهم عَلى تَخَوُّفٍ﴾, that is: or that He seize them after He has made them afraid, by destroying one group so that the one next to it becomes afraid. It was also said: "على تخوّف" means: by gradual diminishing (تنقّص); the meaning of diminishing is that He diminishes them in their wealth and their fruits until He destroys them. It is related that ʿUmar said: "I did not know the meaning of ﴿أوْ يَأْخُذَهم عَلى تَخَوُّفٍ﴾ until I heard the words of the poet:
؎تَخَوَّفَ السَّيْرُ مِنها تامِكًا قَرِدًا كَما تَخَوَّفَ عُودَ النَّبْعَةِ السَّفِنُ
(The journeying wore down (تخوّف) her high, compact hump, as the rasp wears down the wood of the nabʿ tree.)"
He is describing a she-camel, and how the journeying diminishes her hump after it had been firm and full.

His words: ﴿أوْ يَأْخُذَهم عَلى تَخَوُّفٍ فَإنَّ رَبَّكم لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, that is: it is of His mercy that He grants respite and so makes room for repentance.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His words: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إلى ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِن شَيْءٍ يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلالُهُ عَنِ اليَمِينِ﴾; it is also read "تتفيّأ ظلاله" (with tāʾ). ﴿سُجَّدًا﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهم داخِرُونَ﴾: the meaning of "داخرون" is: humbled. This verse requires reflection, and its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is that everything Allah has created, of body, bone, flesh, star and tree, is submissive to Allah, prostrating; and the disbeliever, even if he disbelieves with his heart, his tongue and his intention, the very substance of his body, his bones and his flesh, and all trees and animals, are submissive to Allah, prostrating.

The proof of this is His words: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ والشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ والنُّجُومُ والجِبالُ والشَّجَرُ والدَّوابُّ وكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النّاسِ وكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ العَذابُ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 18]. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: the disbeliever prostrates to other than Allah, while his shadow prostrates to Allah. The interpretation of the shadow is the interpretation of the body that casts the shadow.

His words: ﴿وَهم داخِرُونَ﴾, that is: these things are innately disposed to obedience.

zajjaj:49-49.t:
His words: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ مِن دابَّةٍ والمَلائِكَةُ﴾: the meaning is: to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens, of angels, and whatever is in the earth, of creatures that move, and the angels — that is: the angels of the earth also prostrate. The proof that there are angels in the earth as well is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿ما يَلْفِظُ مِن قَوْلٍ إلا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ﴾ [Qāf: 18]
and His words: ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّباتٌ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ ومِن خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِن أمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 11]
and His words: ﴿وَإنَّ عَلَيْكم لَحافِظِينَ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 10] ﴿كِرامًا﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 11].
His words: ﴿وَهم لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ﴿يَخافُونَ رَبَّهم مِن فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 50], that is: they fear their Lord with the fear of those who are devoted [to Him] and who revere [Him]. ﴿وَيَفْعَلُونَ ما يُؤْمَرُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 50]: He described them with obedience, and that they neither go beyond a command of His nor anticipate it.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
His words: ﴿وَلَهُ الدِّينُ واصِبًا﴾: it was said its meaning is "perpetually", that is: "as obedience binding forever". It is possible — and Allah knows best — that "وله الدين واصبًا" means: "His is the religion and the obedience, whether the servant is pleased with what he is commanded or not, and whether it is easy for him or not"; so His is the religion even if there is toil (الوَصَب) in it, and al-waṣab is severe fatigue. Then He said: ﴿أفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَتَّقُونَ﴾, that is: will you then fear other than Allah — He of whom it has become clear to you that He is One, that He is the Creator of everything, that whatever blessing you have is from Him, and that, had He willed to destroy you when you disbelieved and not to give you respite until the day of repentance, He would have been able? He made known that, despite His establishing the proofs that He is One and His commanding that no god be taken alongside Him, they worshipped others, because they said of the idols: ﴿ما نَعْبُدُهم إلا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إلى اللَّهِ زُلْفى﴾ [al-Zumar: 3].

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that there is no god but He, and that it is not permissible to worship other than Him, even if one intends by that worship to draw near to Allah alone. He, Majestic and Exalted, said: ﴿وَقالَ اللَّهُ لا تَتَّخِذُوا إلَهَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 51]; He mentioned "two (اثنين)" as emphasis (tawkīd) of His word "إلهين" (two gods), just as He mentioned "one" in His words: ﴿إنَّما هو إلَهٌ واحِدٌ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 51].

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His words: ﴿وَما بِكم مِن نِعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ﴾: the fāʾ has entered although there is no verb here, because the bāʾ is connected with a verb; the meaning is: "Whatever blessing has come upon you is from Allah", that is: whatever Allah has given you of bodily health, abundance of provision, or enjoyment of wealth or children — all of that is from Allah.

His words: ﴿ثُمَّ إذا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ فَإلَيْهِ تَجْأرُونَ﴾, that is: to Him you raise your voices in calling for help. One says "جأر الرجل يجأر جؤارًا". Words for sounds are built on the patterns "فُعال" and "فَعِيل": as for fuʿāl, it is like "الصُّراخ" (screaming), "الجُؤار" (crying out) and "البُكاء" (weeping); and as for faʿīl, it is like "العَوِيل" (wailing) and "الزَّئِير" (roaring); and fuʿāl is more common.

zajjaj:54-54.t:
His words: ﴿إذا فَرِيقٌ مِنكم بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: this is specific to those who disbelieved in Him.

His words: ﴿لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهُمْ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 55], that is: so that they disbelieve because We bestowed blessings on them; that is: they made what We provided them and the blessings We bestowed on them a means to disbelief, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿رَبَّنا إنَّكَ آتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ ومَلأهُ زِينَةً وأمْوالا في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا رَبَّنا لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ﴾ [Yūnus: 88]. It may also be that "ليكفروا بما آتيناهم" means: so that they deny Allah's blessing in that, as He said: ﴿أفَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 71].

His words: ﴿فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 55]: Allah, Majestic and Exalted, did not command them to enjoy themselves as a command of worship; it is only the form of a command used as a threat, as He said: ﴿قُلْ آمِنُوا بِهِ أوْ لا تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 107]. That is: Allah has promised, threatened and warned, and the messengers have conveyed; so whoever after that chooses disbelief and the enjoyment of what distances him from Allah will come to know the outcome of his affair. Allah has made clear the outcome of disbelief and disobedience by conclusive proofs and clear signs.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
His words: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِما لا يَعْلَمُونَ نَصِيبًا مِمّا رَزَقْناهُمْ﴾: this is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿فَقالُوا هَذا لِلَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ وهَذا لِشُرَكائِنا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 136]: they assigned a share by which they drew near to Allah, Exalted is He, and a share by which they drew near to the idols and stones.

His words: ﴿تاللَّهِ لَتُسْألُنَّ عَمّا كُنْتُمْ تَفْتَرُونَ﴾, that is: "By Allah, you will surely be asked about it with a questioning of rebuke, until you confess it against yourselves and bind yourselves by the proof."

zajjaj:57-57.t:
His words: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ البَناتِ سُبْحانَهُ﴾: because they claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah. "سبحانه": its meaning is: His being declared free of evil. ﴿وَلَهم ما يَشْتَهُونَ﴾:
"ما" is in the position of the nominative (fī mawḍiʿ rafʿ), and nothing else; the meaning is: "Glory be to Him! And theirs is the thing they desire", as He said: ﴿أمْ لَهُ البَناتُ ولَكُمُ البَنُونَ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 39].

If someone asks: why can the meaning not be "and they assign to themselves (لهم) what they desire" [with "ما" accusative]? It is said: the Arabs use in this position "جعل لنفسه ما يشتهي" (he assigned to himself what he desires); they do not say "جعل زيدٌ له ما يشتهي" when he means himself.

zajjaj:58-58.t: Then He made known that they assign daughters to Allah, saying: ﴿وَإذا بُشِّرَ أحَدُهم بِالأُنْثى ظَلَّ وجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا وهو كَظِيمٌ﴾: so to the One whom they acknowledge as their Creator they assign daughters, whose standing among them is this standing. The meaning of "ظلّ وجهه مسودًّا" is: changed with the change of one who is grieved. Of everyone who meets with something hateful it is said: "His face has become black with grief and sorrow"; and from this is your saying: "I blackened so-and-so's face."

zajjaj:59-59.t: His words: ﴿يَتَوارى مِنَ القَوْمِ مِن سُوءِ ما بُشِّرَ بِهِ﴾: it was said: in the Jāhiliyya, when labour came upon a man's wife, he would hide himself in order to learn what would be born to him. If it was a male he was pleased and delighted with it, and if it was a female he was dejected and saddened by it. Some of them would bury their child alive — bury her living — or keep her in dislike and contempt. So Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿يَتَوارى مِنَ القَوْمِ مِن سُوءِ ما بُشِّرَ بِهِ أيُمْسِكُهُ عَلى هُونٍ أمْ يَدُسُّهُ في التُّرابِ ألا ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ﴾, that is: evil indeed is their judgement in that deed, in their assigning daughters to Allah while assigning sons to themselves, and in their attributing to Allah the taking of a child.

zajjaj:61-61.t:
His words: ﴿وَلَوْ يُؤاخِذُ اللَّهُ النّاسَ بِظُلْمِهِمْ ما تَرَكَ عَلَيْها مِن دابَّةٍ﴾: the meaning of "عليها" is: on the earth. The pronoun indicates the earth because creatures that move are only on the earth.

His words: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ المَثَلُ الأعْلى﴾ [al-Naḥl: 60]: it has come in the exegesis that it is His saying: "There is no god but Allah." Its interpretation is that to Allah, exalted be His praise, belongs the affirmation of oneness and the negation of every god besides Him.

zajjaj:62-62.t:
His words: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ ما يَكْرَهُونَ﴾, that is: they assign to Allah the daughters whom they themselves dislike.

His words: ﴿وَتَصِفُ ألْسِنَتُهُمُ الكَذِبَ أنَّ لَهُمُ الحُسْنى﴾: "أنّ" is a badal (substitute) for "الكذب"; the meaning is: and their tongues describe that theirs is the best, that is: they describe that, despite this ugly deed of theirs, they will have from Allah, exalted be His praise, a good reward.

His words: ﴿لا جَرَمَ أنَّ لَهُمُ النّارَ﴾: "لا" is a rejection of their claim; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: it is not as they described. "جرم أن لهم النار": the meaning is: "this deed of theirs has earned (جرم) that theirs is the Fire", that is: "their deed has earned that theirs is the Fire". It was also said that "أنّ" is in the position of the nominative; Quṭrub mentioned that, and said: the meaning is that theirs is the Fire.

﴿وَأنَّهم مُفْرَطُونَ﴾: there are four ways [of reading] it: "مُفْرَطون", with sukūn on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ; "مُفَرَّطون", with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the rāʾ doubled and with fatḥa; "مُفْرِطون", with sukūn on the fāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ; and "مُفَرِّطون", with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the rāʾ doubled and with kasra. As for the explanation of "مفرَطون" and "مفرَّطون", it has come from Ibn ʿAbbās: "left behind (متروكون)", and it was also reported from him: "hastened forward (معجَلون)".

The meaning of "الفَرْط" in the language is going ahead; "قد فرط إليّ منه قول" means: a word from him reached me beforehand. So the meaning of "مفرَطون" is: sent ahead to the Fire, and likewise "مفرَّطون". Whoever explained it as "left behind" is also [consistent with] that, that is: they have been made to go ahead into the punishment forever, left in it. Whoever read "مفرِّطون", the meaning is that it describes them as having fallen short (فرّطوا) in this world, not working in it for the Hereafter; this reading is confirmed by His words: ﴿أنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يا حَسْرَتا عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ في جَنْبِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 56]. Whoever read "مفرِطون", the meaning is that they went to excess (أفرطوا) in disobeying Allah, as you say: "قد أفرط فلان في مكروهي" (so-and-so has gone to excess in what harms me); its interpretation is that he preferred incapacity and put it forward.

zajjaj:64-64.t: His words: ﴿وَما أنْـزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الكِتابَ إلا لِتُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ الَّذِي اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ وهُدًى ورَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, with "رحمةً" in the accusative: the meaning is: "And We have not sent down to you the Book except as guidance and mercy", that is: We sent it down to you only for guidance and mercy; so it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). "وهدًى ورحمةٌ" [in the nominative] is also grammatically possible in this position; the meaning would be: "And We have not sent down to you the Book except for clarification, and it is — besides that — guidance and mercy."

zajjaj:66-66.t:
﴿وَإنَّ لَكم في الأنْعامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكم مِمّا في بُطُونِهِ﴾; it is also read "نَسقيكم". One says "سقيته" and "أسقيته" with one meaning. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl said: "سقيته" is as you say "I handed it to him and he drank", while "أسقيته" is "I provided him with drink (made a watering for him)". Likewise the words of the poet, which can bear both views:
؎سَقى قَوْمِي بَنِي مَجْدٍ وأسْقى نُمَيْرًا والقَبائِلَ مِن هِلالِ
(May He give drink (سقى) to my people, the Banū Majd, and give drink (أسقى) to Numayr and the tribes of Hilāl.)
The grammarians cited this verse on the basis that "سقى" and "أسقى" have one meaning, but it can bear the second explanation. "الأنعام" has the form of a plural but is a generic noun (ism li-l-jins), treated as masculine and feminine: one says "هو الأنعام" and "هي الأنعام". [Here:] "نسقيكم مما في بطونه" (in its bellies, masculine), and in another place: "مما في بطونها" (feminine). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that in His bringing forth milk from between dung and blood there is proof of a power of which no one is capable except Allah, like whom there is nothing.

zajjaj:67-67.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمِن ثَمَراتِ النَّخِيلِ والأعْنابِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنهُ سَكَرًا ورِزْقًا حَسَنًا إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾, that is: in what We have made clear there is a sign pointing to the oneness of Allah. In explaining His words ﴿سَكَرًا ورِزْقًا حَسَنًا﴾ they said: it is wine, before it was forbidden, and "the good provision" is what is eaten of grapes and dates. It was also said that the meaning of "السَّكَر" is food (الطُّعم), and they recited:
؎جَعَلَتْ أعْراضَ الكِرامِ سَكَرا
(You have made the honour of noble men a "sakar".)
that is: you made their blood food for yourself. But this is closer to the first explanation; the meaning is: you have taken to intoxicating yourself with the honour of noble men, and this is clearer, in what is said of "one who [يتبرك] in people's honour". [Translator's note: the word يتبرك ("seeks blessing") appears to be corrupt in the text; translated as written.]

zajjaj:68-68.t:
His words: ﴿وَأوْحى رَبُّكَ إلى النَّحْلِ أنِ اتَّخِذِي مِنَ الجِبالِ بُيُوتًا﴾; also "بِيوتًا". Whoever reads "بُيوتًا" with ḍamma follows the regular pattern (al-qiyās), like "كَعب / كُعوب" and "قَلب / قُلوب". As for whoever reads "بِيوتًا" with kasra, none of the Basrans has mentioned anything like it, because they do not allow its like: there is no pattern "فِعُل" or "فِعُول" in the language. Those who read it so changed the ḍamma into kasra because of the yāʾ that follows it.

The meaning of "الوحي" in the language is of two kinds, which go back to the meaning of informing and making understood. Of al-waḥy is Allah's revelation to His prophets, through what the angels heard of His speech; and of it is inspiration (الإلهام), as Allah said: ﴿وَأخْرَجَتِ الأرْضُ أثْقالَها﴾ [al-Zalzala: 2], up to: ﴿بِأنَّ رَبَّكَ أوْحى لَها﴾ [al-Zalzala: 5]; its meaning is: He inspired it. So Allah has inspired every creature and every being with a soul to seek out what benefits it and avoid what harms it, and of that He mentioned the matter of the bees. The singular of "النحل" is "نحلة", like "نخل / نخلة" (palm trees / a palm tree). [He mentioned them] because in them there is such subtle workmanship and marvellous creation as constitutes the greatest lesson: He inspired them to take dwellings and homes, and to eat of all fruits despite the difference of their tastes.

zajjaj:69-69.t:
Then He made the way to that easy for them, and said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ثُمَّ كُلِي مِن كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ فاسْلُكِي سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلا﴾, that is: Allah has made them smooth for you and made their paths easy for you. Then He said: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِن بُطُونِها شَرابٌ مُخْتَلِفٌ ألْوانُهُ﴾: they eat what is sour, what is bitter, and what has an indescribable taste, and Allah transforms that into honey, which comes out of their bellies — although they cast it out of their mouths. But He said ﴿مِن بُطُونِها﴾ because the transformation of foods only takes place in the bellies, and some of it comes out of the mouth, like the constant saliva that comes out of the mouth of the son of Adam; so the bees bring the honey out of their bellies to their mouths.

﴿فِيهِ شِفاءٌ لِلنّاسِ﴾: there are two views on this. It was said that the hāʾ (the pronoun "it") refers to the honey; the meaning is: "In the honey there is healing for people." And it was said that the hāʾ is for the Quran; the meaning is: "In the Quran there is healing for people." This view, when it is explained, is known to be good; the meaning is: "In what We have related to you of the story of the bees in the Quran, and the other stories which show that Allah is One, there is healing for people." But the explanation as honey is very good.

If someone objects: we have seen people whom honey benefits and people whom honey harms, so how can there be healing for people in it? The answer to this is to say to him: water is the life of everything, yet we have seen people whom water kills when they take it in the presence of some illness in the body. And we have seen the healing of honey in most of these drinks, because julep (الجلّاب) and oxymel (السكنجبين) have honey as their base, and likewise all the electuaries. This objection concerning honey is only the objection of ignorant people who do not know its worth in benefit; as for whoever knows the extent of its benefit, even if he is not of the people of this religion, he does not deny that there is healing in honey.

zajjaj:70-70.t: His words: ﴿واللَّهُ خَلَقَكم ثُمَّ يَتَوَفّاكم ومِنكم مَن يُرَدُّ إلى أرْذَلِ العُمُرِ لِكَيْ لا يَعْلَمَ بَعْدَ عِلْمٍ شَيْئًا﴾, that is: among you is one who grows old and advanced in age until his mind goes through dotage, so that after having been knowing he becomes ignorant. The meaning — and Allah knows best — of "لكيلا يعلم بعد علم شيئًا" is: in order to show you of His power that, just as He is able to make him die and to give him life, He is able to move him from knowledge to ignorance. He, Mighty and Majestic, made known that death and life are in His hand, and that a person may nourish himself with foods by which he aims at the utmost in soundness and survival, yet he is unable to add anything to the measure of his term.

zajjaj:71-71.t:
His words: ﴿واللَّهُ فَضَّلَ بَعْضَكم عَلى بَعْضٍ في الرِّزْقِ فَما الَّذِينَ فُضِّلُوا بِرادِّي رِزْقِهِمْ عَلى ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهم فَهم فِيهِ سَواءٌ﴾, that is: Allah has favoured the owners over their slaves, and made the slave unable to own [property] along with his master; and He made known that the owner does not give back to his slave of the surplus in his hand until their condition in ownership becomes equal. It was said to them: "You are all of the children of Adam, and you do not make yourselves equal in what your right hands possess, though you are all human beings; so how can you assign part of the provision that Allah has provided you to Him and part of it to your idols, making Allah and the idols partners, when you do not accept partnership for yourselves with one who is like you?"

His words: ﴿أفَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ﴾: there are two ways of taking it. It may mean: "Is it because Allah has bestowed blessings on you that you have taken the blessings as a means to deny [Him] and to associate the idols with Him?!" And it may be that "أفبنعمة الله" means: "Is it what Allah has bestowed on you — His making clear to you what you need — that you deny?!"

zajjaj:72-72.t:
His words: ﴿واللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكم مِن أنْفُسِكم أزْواجًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that Allah created Eve from one of the ribs of Adam; that is the meaning of "He made for you from yourselves spouses", that is: from your own kind.

His words: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكم مِن أزْواجِكم بَنِينَ وحَفَدَةً﴾: people differed over the explanation of al-ḥafada. It was said: children; it was said: daughters; it was said: sons-in-law; it was said: in-laws; and it was said: helpers. The reality of this is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made from the spouses sons, and those who help with what is needed quickly and obediently. One says "حفد يحفد حفدًا وحفَدًا وحفَدانًا" when one hastens. The poet said:
؎حَفَدَ الوَلائِدُ حَوْلَهُنَّ وأسْلَمَتْ بِأكُفِّهِنَّ أزِمَّةَ الأجْمالِ
(The serving girls hastened around them, and the camels' reins were surrendered into their hands.)
Its meaning is: they hastened in service.

zajjaj:74-74.t: His words: ﴿فَلا تَضْرِبُوا لِلَّهِ الأمْثالَ﴾, that is: do not set up any likeness to Allah, because He is One, without any like, Majestic and Mighty, and there is no god but He, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:75-75.t: Then He struck the parable for them, and said: ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا عَبْدًا مَمْلُوكًا لا يَقْدِرُ عَلى شَيْءٍ ومَن رَزَقْناهُ مِنّا رِزْقًا حَسَنًا فَهو يُنْفِقُ مِنهُ سِرًّا وجَهْرًا هَلْ يَسْتَوُونَ﴾. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that two who are equal in creation, when one of them is able to spend, an owner, and the other is incapable, unable to spend, are not equal; so how then [can there be equality] between stones that neither move nor understand and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who has power over everything and who is the Provider of all His creation? Thus He made clear to them their error and their remoteness from the road in their worship of idols.

zajjaj:76-76.t:
Then He added further clarification, and said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا رَجُلَيْنِ أحَدُهُما أبْكَمُ لا يَقْدِرُ عَلى شَيْءٍ﴾. "الأبكم" is the one completely shut off, who neither hears, nor sees, nor understands. Then He said: ﴿وَهُوَ كَلٌّ عَلى مَوْلاهُ﴾, that is: on his guardian. ﴿أيْنَما يُوَجِّهْهُ لا يَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي هو ومَن يَأْمُرُ بِالعَدْلِ وهو عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾,
that is: are the capable one with full discernment and the incapable one who perceives nothing and brings no good equal?! So how can they make Allah and stones equal?!

zajjaj:77-77.t: His words: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: to Allah belongs the knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. ﴿وَما أمْرُ السّاعَةِ إلا كَلَمْحِ البَصَرِ﴾: "the Hour (الساعة)" is a name for the causing of creation to die and bringing them back to life. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the resurrection and the bringing back to life, within His power and will, are like the blink of an eye, or nearer. He does not mean that the Hour will come in less than the blink of an eye; rather, He is describing the swiftness of the power to bring it about.

zajjaj:78-78.t: His words: ﴿واللَّهُ أخْرَجَكم مِن بُطُونِ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ﴾; also "إمّهاتكم" with kasra. The original form of "الأمّهات" is "أُمّات", but the hāʾ was added for emphasis, just as they added a hāʾ in their saying "أهرقتُ الماء" (I poured out the water), whose original form is "أرقتُ الماء". "الأفئدة" is the plural of "فؤاد" (heart), like "غراب / أغربة" (crow / crows); "فؤاد" was not given the plural of greater number: "فِئدان" is not said, as "غِربان" is said for "غراب". Then He, Glory be to Him, pointed them to His power over the matter of the Hour by what they witnessed of His governance, and said: ﴿ألَمْ يَرَوْا إلى الطَّيْرِ مُسَخَّراتٍ في جَوِّ السَّماءِ ما يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إلا اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 79]. "جوّ السماء" is the air far from the earth; farther than it from the earth is al-sukāk, and like al-sukāk is al-lawḥ; the singular of al-sukāk is "سُكاكة".

zajjaj:80-80.t:
His words: ﴿واللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكم مِن بُيُوتِكم سَكَنًا﴾, that is: a place in which you dwell. ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكم مِن جُلُودِ الأنْعامِ بُيُوتًا﴾: "الأنعام" is a name for camels, cattle and sheep.

His words: ﴿تَسْتَخِفُّونَها يَوْمَ ظَعْنِكم ويَوْمَ إقامَتِكُمْ﴾: the meaning of "تستخفّونها" is: carrying them is light for you on your journeys and in your stays. It is read "يوم ظَعْنكم" and "ظَعَنكم". ﴿وَمِن أصْوافِها وأوْبارِها وأشْعارِها أثاثًا ومَتاعًا إلى حِينٍ﴾: "الأوبار" (soft hair) belongs to camels, "الأصواف" (wool) to sheep, and "الأشعار" (hair) to goats. "الأثاث" is household goods; household goods are also called "الأُهَرة". One says "قد أثّ يئِثّ أثًّا" when someone comes to have household goods.

zajjaj:81-81.t:
His words: ﴿واللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكم مِمّا خَلَقَ ظِلالا﴾, that is: He has made for you, of trees, that by which you take shade, and made for you, of the mountains, shelters (أكنان). The singular of "الأكنان" is "كِنّ", on the pattern of "حِمل / أحمال"; its singular cannot be "كِنان", because the plural of "الكِنان" is "أكِنّة". That is: He made for you what shelters you. ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكم سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾: everything you wear is a "سربال", whether shirt, coat of mail, breastplate or other. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿سَرابِيلُهم مِن قَطِرانٍ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 50]. He said ﴿تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾ and did not say "that protect you from cold", because what protects from heat protects from cold.

His words: ﴿وَسَرابِيلَ تَقِيكم بَأْسَكُمْ﴾, that is: He made for you coats of mail with which you protect yourselves in wars from the violence of iron and the like.

His words: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكم لَعَلَّكم تُسْلِمُونَ﴾: most readings have "تُسلِمون" (you may submit), and it is also read "لعلكم تَسلَمون", that is: "so that when you wear coats of mail in war you may be safe (سلمتم) from wounds."

zajjaj:82-82.t: Then He said, after making the signs clear to them: ﴿فَإنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإنَّما عَلَيْكَ البَلاغُ المُبِينُ﴾, that is: upon you it is to convey the message and to bring the signs that point to prophethood.

zajjaj:83-83.t: His words: ﴿يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنْكِرُونَها﴾, that is: they know that the matter of the Prophet ﷺ is true, then they deny that.

zajjaj:86-86.t: His words: ﴿فَألْقَوْا إلَيْهِمُ القَوْلَ إنَّكم لَكاذِبُونَ﴾, that is: when those who associated partners saw that what they used to associate with Allah was of no benefit to them, and their gods disowned them, as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿كَلا سَيَكْفُرُونَ بِعِبادَتِهِمْ ويَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدًّا﴾ [Maryam: 82]. [Translator's note: the sentence beginning "when…" has no main clause in the text; translated as written.]

zajjaj:88-88.t: His words: ﴿زِدْناهم عَذابًا فَوْقَ العَذابِ بِما كانُوا يُفْسِدُونَ﴾: it is related in the exegesis that what they were given in addition is scorpions with fangs like tall palm trees. It was also said that they go out from the heat of the Fire to the bitter cold (الزمهرير), and from the severity of its cold they rush back to the Fire.

zajjaj:89-89.t:
His words: ﴿وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ في كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا عَلَيْهِمْ مِن أنْفُسِهِمْ﴾: every prophet is a witness against his community, and he is the most just witness against it.

His words: ﴿وَنَـزَّلْنا عَلَيْكَ الكِتابَ تِبْيانًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾:
"تِبيانًا" is a noun with the meaning of al-bayān (clarification); like "التِّبيان" is "التِّلقاء". If it were read "تَبيانًا", on the pattern "تَفعال", that would be a [grammatically] valid form, because "التَّبيان" has the meaning of "التَّبيين"; but reciting it so is not permitted, because none of the Quran readers has read it so.

zajjaj:91-91.t: His words: ﴿وَلا تَنْقُضُوا الأيْمانَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِها﴾: one says "وكّدتُ الأمر" and "أكّدتُ الأمر" (I confirmed the matter); they are two good dialect forms. The original is the wāw, and the hamza is a substitute for it.

zajjaj:92-92.t:
His words: ﴿وَلا تَكُونُوا كالَّتِي نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَها مِن بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ أنْكاثًا﴾: "أنكاثًا" is accusative because it has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), since the meaning of "نكثتُ" is "نقضتُ" (I undid), and the meaning of "نقضتُ" is "نكثتُ". The singular of "الأنقاض" [Translator's note: so in the text; the context requires "الأنكاث"] is "نِكث", which is what is unravelled after it has been spun. The poet said:
؎تَرْعِيَّةٌ تَعْرِفُ الأرْباعَ ضَجْعَتُهُ لَهُ نِكاثٌ مِنَ الأنْجادِ والفُضَلِ
(A skilled herdsman, whose lying-down place the spring encampments know; he has unravelled strands (نكاث) of cushions and loose garments.)
His words: ﴿تَتَّخِذُونَ أيْمانَكم دَخَلا بَيْنَكُمْ﴾, that is: as deceit and rancour among you. "دخلًا" is accusative because it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "you take your oaths for deceit and corruption (الدَّخَل)". Of everything into which a defect has entered it is said: "it is مدخول (corrupted)" and "there is دَخَل in it".

His words: ﴿أنْ تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هي أرْبى مِن أُمَّةٍ﴾: so that one of them may be deluded by the other. "أربى" is taken from "ربا الشيء يربو" when a thing becomes abundant.

zajjaj:96-96.t:
His words: ﴿ما عِنْدَكم يَنْفَدُ وما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ باقٍ﴾: one says "نفِد الشيء ينفَد نفادًا ونفَدًا" when it comes to an end.

His words: ﴿فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَياةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ [al-Naḥl: 97]: it was said: "We shall surely provide him with what is lawful"; and it was said: "a good life" is Paradise. [On His words "أن تكون أمة هي أربى من أمة":] the position of "أربى" is nominative; the meaning is: "that one community be more numerous than another". Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the position of "أربى" is accusative and that "هي" is an ʿimād (support pronoun). This is a mistake: "هي" does not come in as ʿimād or faṣl (separating pronoun) with indefinite nouns. He likened it to His words: ﴿تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هو خَيْرًا وأعْظَمَ أجْرًا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20]; but in "تجدوه" the hāʾ is definite, while "أمّة" is indefinite.

zajjaj:98-98.t: His words: ﴿فَإذا قَرَأْتَ القُرْآنَ فاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ الرَّجِيمِ﴾: its meaning is: when you want to recite the Quran, seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan. Its meaning is not "seek refuge with Allah after you recite", because seeking refuge was commanded before beginning. This is used in ordinary speech; its like is: "When you eat, say: In the name of Allah." Its like in the Quran is: ﴿إذا قُمْتُمْ إلى الصَّلاةِ فاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 6]: the preparation is before the prayer, and the meaning is: "When you intend that, then do …".

zajjaj:101-101.t: His words: ﴿وَإذا بَدَّلْنا آيَةً مَكانَ آيَةٍ واللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِما يُنَـزِّلُ﴾, that is: when a verse was abrogated by another verse in which there was hardship for them, ﴿قالُوا إنَّما أنْتَ مُفْتَرٍ﴾, that is: they said: you have lied to us.

zajjaj:103-103.t:
His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أنَّهم يَقُولُونَ إنَّما يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed His Prophet ﷺ of what they were saying among themselves.

His words: ﴿لِسانُ الَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إلَيْهِ أعْجَمِيٌّ﴾; it is also read "يَلحَدون", that is: "the tongue of the one to whom they incline the speech is foreign". It was said: this was a slave boy belonging to Ḥuwayṭib, named ʿĀyish, who became Muslim and was excellent in his Islam.

﴿وَهَذا لِسانٌ عَرَبِيٌّ مُبِينٌ﴾: one says "عرُب الإنسان يعرُب عُروبيّةً وعَرابةً وعُروبةً" (a person became an Arab in speech).

His words: ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾: He described it with clarity, just as He described it as Arabic. The meaning of "عربي" is that its speaker speaks Arabic; and its meaning is: expressing clearly (مُعرِب), making plain (مُبين).

zajjaj:105-105.t: His words: ﴿إنَّما يَفْتَرِي الكَذِبَ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الكاذِبُونَ﴾, that is: the only ones who fabricate lies are those who, when they see the signs of which none but Allah is capable, deny them; these are the most lying of liars.

zajjaj:106-106.t: His words: ﴿مَن كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ إيمانِهِ إلا مَن أُكْرِهَ وقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالإيمانِ﴾: "مَن" is in the position of the nominative (fī mawḍiʿ rafʿ) as a badal (substitute) for "الكاذبون" (the liars), explaining "الكاذبون". "مَن" cannot be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), because there is no khabar (predicate) here for the mubtadaʾ, since His words ﴿مَن كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ إيمانِهِ إلا مَن أُكْرِهَ وقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالإيمانِ﴾ are not a complete statement. After it comes: ﴿وَلَكِنْ مَن شَرَحَ بِالكُفْرِ صَدْرًا فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾, and His words ﴿فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ are the khabar of the "مَن" that comes after "لكن".

zajjaj:109-109.t: His words: ﴿لا جَرَمَ أنَّهم في الآخِرَةِ هُمُ الخاسِرُونَ﴾: "أنّ" may be in the position of the nominative, on the basis that "لا" is a rejection of the [preceding] speech, and the meaning is: "It is established (وجب) that they …". And "أنّ" may be in the position of the accusative, on the basis that the meaning is: "This deed of theirs has earned (جرم) that in the Hereafter they are the losers." The meaning of "جرم" is "earned", and "المجرم" is the one who earns; it is mostly used of sins.

zajjaj:110-110.t: His words: ﴿ثُمَّ إنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا مِن بَعْدِ ما فُتِنُوا ثُمَّ جاهَدُوا وصَبَرُوا إنَّ رَبَّكَ مِن بَعْدِها لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, that is: after the deed which they did. This verse concerns the story of ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and his companions, when the people of Mecca tortured them and compelled them to abandon faith, and they disbelieved with their tongues while faith was in their hearts and intentions. Then they fled from them and emigrated to the Prophet ﷺ; a party of the people of Mecca overtook them and fought them until Allah saved them from them, and they persevered in fighting them.

zajjaj:111-111.t: His words: ﴿يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجادِلُ عَنْ نَفْسِها﴾: "يوم" is accusative on one of two grounds: in the sense of "your Lord, after that, is Forgiving, Merciful on the day when [every soul] comes"; or it may be in the sense of "remember", because the purpose of the Quran is admonition, warning and reminding, that is: "Remember the day when every soul comes", that is: every person pleading for himself. It is related that when the Day of Resurrection comes, Hell will give a sigh, and there will remain no angel brought near nor prophet sent but will fall on his knees and say: "O Lord, myself, myself!" This is confirmed by His words, Exalted is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ المَرْءُ مِن أخِيهِ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 34] ﴿وَأُمِّهِ وأبِيهِ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 35], to the end of the passage.

zajjaj:112-112.t: His words: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا قَرْيَةً كانَتْ آمِنَةً مُطْمَئِنَّةً﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "And Allah struck a parable: the parable of a town that was secure and at rest." ﴿يَأْتِيها رِزْقُها رَغَدًا مِن كُلِّ مَكانٍ﴾, that is: abundantly from every place. What has come in the exegesis is that He means by it Mecca. That is because they had become secure from hunger and fear, since Allah, exalted be His praise, made the hearts of people incline towards them, so their provisions came to them in their own land; it was a secure sanctuary, while people were being snatched away all around them. ﴿فَكَفَرَتْ بِأنْعُمِ اللَّهِ فَأذاقَها اللَّهُ لِباسَ الجُوعِ والخَوْفِ﴾: they went hungry until they came to eating camel hair with blood, and hunger brought them to a state beyond which there is no further limit. "أنعُم" is the plural of "نِعمة" (blessing), and they said [similarly]: "شِدّة / أشُدّ". Quṭrub said: it may be the plural of "نُعم", "نُعم / أنعُم" being like "بُؤس / أبؤُس".

zajjaj:113-113.t:
His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جاءَهم رَسُولٌ مِنهم فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأخَذَهُمُ العَذابُ وهم ظالِمُونَ﴾: Allah punished them with the sword and killing.

His words: ﴿وَلا تَقُولُوا لِما تَصِفُ ألْسِنَتُكُمُ الكَذِبَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 116]: there are three ways [of reading] "الكذب": it has been read "الكَذِبَ", it has been read "الكُذُبُ", and it has been read "الكَذِبِ". Whoever reads "الكَذِبَ" — and this is the majority reading — the meaning is: "And do not say, because of your tongues' describing the lie: ﴿هَذا حَلالٌ وهَذا حَرامٌ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 116]". Whoever reads "الكَذِبِ" makes it refer back to "ما" [as its badal]; the meaning is: "And do not say, because of your tongues' describing of the lie". And whoever reads "الكُذُبُ", it is a naʿt (adjective) of the tongues: one says "لسان كذوب" (a lying tongue) and "ألسنة كُذُب" (lying tongues). This was said to them only because of what they had forbidden and permitted, saying: ﴿ما في بُطُونِ هَذِهِ الأنْعامِ خالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنا ومُحَرَّمٌ عَلى أزْواجِنا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 139]; we have explained that in its place.

zajjaj:117-117.t: His words: ﴿مَتاعٌ قَلِيلٌ﴾: the meaning is: "This enjoyment of theirs, which they have done, is a little enjoyment." If it were outside the Quran, the accusative "متاعًا قليلًا" would be permissible in it, on the basis that the meaning is: "they enjoy themselves thus, a little enjoyment".

zajjaj:120-120.t:
His words: ﴿إنَّ إبْراهِيمَ كانَ أُمَّةً قانِتًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that he believed alone; and most of the exegesis has it that he was a teacher of good, and a ḥanīf leader. It was said: he adopted circumcision. Its real meaning in the language is that "الحنيف" is one who inclines to a thing and never departs from it; so he, peace be upon him, was inclined to Islam, never departing from it. They said of "القانت": he is the obedient one; and "القانت" is the one who carries out the whole of the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

His words: ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ﴾: "لم يكُ" is originally "لم يكن"; according to Sībawayh the nūn was dropped only because of the frequent use of this word. The leading Basrans mentioned that several things combined in it: frequency of use; that it [i.e. kāna] is an expression for every action, past and future; and that, in addition, it [i.e. the nūn] resembles the soft letters (ḥurūf al-līn), because it serves as a marker just as the soft letters serve as markers, and it is a nasal sound (ghunna) that comes out of the nose. For that reason it tolerated being dropped.

zajjaj:124-124.t: His words: ﴿إنَّما جُعِلَ السَّبْتُ عَلى الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ﴾: the speech shows that they were made bound by the sign of the prophethood of Moses, peace be upon him. It has come in the exegesis that some of them forbade it and some of them permitted it, and this is the most indicative of what has come concerning the disagreement over the Sabbath. It has also come frequently in the exegesis that they were commanded to take a festival, and they opposed and said: we want the day of the Sabbath, because it is the last day, on which the creation of the heavens and the earth was finished; and that Jesus commanded the Christians to take Friday as a festival, and they said: our festival shall only be after the festival of the Jews, so they made it Sunday. Allah knows best the truth of that.

zajjaj:125-125.t: His words: ﴿ادْعُ إلى سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِالحِكْمَةِ والمَوْعِظَةِ الحَسَنَةِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis: "wisdom" is prophethood, and "the admonition" is the Quran. ﴿وَجادِلْهم بِالَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ﴾, that is: argue with them without being harsh or hard-hearted in that; be gentle towards them.

zajjaj:126-126.t:
﴿وَإنْ عاقَبْتُمْ فَعاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ ما عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾: the first was called "punishment (عقوبة)", although only the second is punishment, for the sake of pairing in the speech (izdiwāj al-kalām), because the two kinds of act have one meaning. Its like is: ﴿وَجَزاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُها﴾ [al-Shūrā: 40]: the second is not an evil deed, but it was called so in order that the wording agree, because the meaning of killing is one. We have explained the parallel of this in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, on His words: ﴿وَمَكَرُوا ومَكَرَ اللَّهُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 54]. It has come in the exegesis that the Muslims intended to mutilate the idolaters, because they had mutilated them; the Muslims intended to exceed them in mutilation, and they were commanded not to exceed. It is possible — and Allah knows best — that the meaning of ﴿وَجَزاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُها﴾ [al-Shūrā: 40] is: whoever has had done to him something for which retaliation is due, let him not exceed retaliation, except by the like.

His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَئِنْ صَبَرْتُمْ لَهو خَيْرٌ لِلصّابِرِينَ﴾: this is like His words: ﴿فَمَن عَفا وأصْلَحَ فَأجْرُهُ عَلى اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 40].

zajjaj:127-127.t: His words: ﴿وَلا تَكُ في ضَيْقٍ مِمّا يَمْكُرُونَ﴾: "ضَيْق" has the meaning of "ضَيِّق" (narrow), lightened, like "مَيْت" and "مَيِّت" (dead). It may also have the meaning of "الضِّيق" (distress), in which case it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of your saying "ضاق الشيء يضيق ضَيقًا" (the thing became narrow).

zajjaj:128-128.t: His words: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا والَّذِينَ هم مُحْسِنُونَ﴾, that is: "Allah is their helper", as He said: ﴿لا تَحْزَنْ إنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنا﴾ [al-Tawba: 40]. So in this verse He has promised help.
